guides.title: Vacuum-bleed the 5.2L clutch hydraulic system
guides.summary: Bleed the clutch through the brake/clutch reservoir, then verify consistent pedal effort, clutch pedal reserve and normal operation.
guides.introduction: The clutch hydraulic circuit transfers pedal movement through fluid to operate the clutch. Trapped air can compress and interfere with that transfer, making pedal response inconsistent. This procedure applies vacuum at the shared brake/clutch reservoir, followed by fluid-level checks and repeated pedal operation.
guides.why: Correctly seated hydraulic tubes, a fully raised pedal and a sealed reservoir adapter establish the starting conditions. Restoring the fluid level between cycles and checking pedal response show whether the bleeding sequence has achieved its intended result.

when.summary: When clutch hydraulic service or diagnosis calls for air removal.
notes: An inconsistent pedal is a reason to investigate; it does not identify a failed component by itself.

prepare.title: Arrange the reservoir vacuum equipment
prepare.detail: Use a suitable bleeder kit, Vacuum Pump Kit 416-D002 and the listed brake/clutch system pressure bleeder/filler. The reservoir stopper must seal tightly. The stated alternative is a 50 mm rubber stopper fitted with an 8 mm pipe.

prepare.title: Use the specified fluid
prepare.detail: Have Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid, PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2. Read the product label and available material safety data sheet before handling.

steps.title: Establish the starting conditions
steps.body: Check that every hydraulic tube is correctly seated and the clutch pedal is at its uppermost position. Check the brake/clutch reservoir and fill it to MAX with the specified fluid.

steps.title: Apply and release reservoir vacuum
steps.body: Fit the tightly sealing stopper and vacuum equipment. Hold the stopper in place while drawing 15–20 inches of vacuum. Maintain that vacuum for one minute, then release it quickly and remove the equipment.

steps.title: Refill and cycle the clutch
steps.body: Recheck the reservoir, restore the level to MAX and install its cap. Press and release the clutch pedal 10 to 12 times, or until effort is consistent and positive at the top of travel. Repeat the vacuum, refill and pedal-cycling sequence two additional times, or until that pedal response is achieved.

steps.title: Complete the operating checks
steps.body: Ensure the reservoir cap is installed. Check clutch pedal reserve and test the clutch system for normal operation. Consistent pedal effort is one completion condition; the reserve and operation checks must also be completed.

watchFor.title: Fluid on paint or plastic
watchFor.body: Brake fluid can damage these surfaces. Immediately wash any spill off with water.

watchFor.title: A loose reservoir stopper
watchFor.body: The adapter requires a tight fit and must be held in place during vacuum application.

notes: Use the vacuum sequence described here even though the listed general equipment includes a pressure bleeder/filler.
The TR3160 installation uses this shared hydraulic bleeding procedure. The base-engine MT82 clutch has its own maintenance guide.

diagnostics.finding: Pedal effort remains inconsistent or is not positive at the top of travel.
diagnostics.meaning: The specified pedal-response endpoint has not been achieved.
diagnostics.next: Continue the prescribed vacuum, refill and pedal-cycling sequence; do not mark bleeding complete solely because vacuum was applied.

verification.title: Confirm the final pedal response
verification.body: Verify consistent, positive effort at the top of clutch pedal travel.

verification.title: Record the operating result
verification.body: Record the clutch pedal reserve check and normal-operation test outcome.

procedures.purpose: Shared clutch-reservoir vacuum bleeding sequence, specified fluid and final pedal/operation checks.
TR3160 installation explicitly requires the shared clutch filling and bleeding procedure after hydraulic connection work.

applicability.equipment: 5.2L with TR3160 manual transmission

authoring.reviewNote: TR3160 installation explicitly references the shared bleeding procedure; corrected inherited MT82 title for this 5.2L-only guide.

guides.title: Find hidden connector and harness faults
guides.summary: Inspect terminal seating, contact fit and concealed harness damage before replacing a component for an intermittent electrical fault.
guides.introduction: A connector can look joined while a terminal behind its seal is loose, a locking tab is displaced, or a contact has been spread by a probe. These faults interrupt a circuit without necessarily leaving an obvious external mark. The illustrations show what a physical inspection can reveal and help separate connector damage from a failed module or sensor.
guides.why: Repeatedly replacing the connected component will not repair a poor terminal fit or a wire that intermittently touches another circuit. The inspection needs to protect the contact springs as well as find the original fault: an unsuitable probe can create another intermittent connection.

when.summary: When an electrical concern is intermittent or a circuit test points to connector contact or hidden harness damage.
notes: This is a condition-based inspection, not a scheduled replacement of connectors.

prepare.title: Identify the circuit and service limits
prepare.detail: Use the correct connector face and circuit information before inspection. Airbag and seat-belt pretensioner terminals are outside individual-terminal repair: do not remove, repair or replace their individual pins. Use the service connector pigtail intended for the affected restraint component, following its restraint-service procedure.

prepare.title: Use a matching contact and suitable probes
prepare.detail: Use the matching service terminal when assessing female contact fit. For test equipment, the linked terminal procedure specifies Rotunda Flex Probes NUD105-R025D or Terminal Probe Kit 29-011A to avoid damaging the contact.

prepare.title: Preserve terminal plating
prepare.detail: For non-restraint connections with gold-plated terminals, use a gold-plated replacement or the specified universal silver- or tin-plated service kit supplied with grease. Do not assume any unplated replacement is equivalent.

steps.title: Check seating behind the seal
steps.body: Compare the locked and unlocked terminal drawings. Pull each wire at the connector end to check whether its terminal is retained; the wire seal can conceal an unlocked terminal that only makes intermittent contact.

steps.title: Verify that the connector halves lock
steps.body: Inspect for a partially joined connector or displaced locking tab, then pull on the connector to verify that its lock holds. A seal or an apparently close fit is not proof that the halves are fully locked.

steps.title: Inspect the stripped wire and crimp
steps.body: Look for insulation left in the connection, missing wire strands, and insulation pierced in a way that creates intermittent contact. Compare the damaged examples with the proper-crimp illustration rather than judging only the outside of the terminal.

steps.title: Assess contact fit without spreading it
steps.body: Insert the correct mating service terminal and check for a loose fit. The terminal-inspection procedure describes unusually low separation force as evidence of damage; a guide or retainer that adds drag can conceal that result and may need removal as directed. Do not push an arbitrary meter probe into a female contact.

steps.title: Inspect the harness around the suspected short
steps.body: Look for the illustrated hidden failures: a solder-coated strand contacting ground or piercing another circuit’s insulation beneath protective wrapping. Keep the grounding foil and the circuit positions in view when interpreting the damage.

steps.title: Select the correct repair route
steps.body: For an ordinary serviceable connector, use the connector-specific terminal release method and matching service parts. Mark the release tool at the depth given for that exact connector before releasing a terminal. If the affected connector belongs to a restraint component, follow its service-pigtail route instead of individual-terminal work.

watchFor.title: Probe damage
watchFor.body: An enlarged female contact can still touch the male pin yet lose reliable spring pressure. A test that forces in an oversized probe may create the very problem being investigated.

watchFor.title: A seal hiding a loose terminal
watchFor.body: A terminal can sit behind an intact seal without being locked into its housing.

watchFor.title: Restraint connector limits
watchFor.body: Airbag and seat-belt pretensioner terminals are outside individual-terminal repair: do not remove, repair or replace their individual pins. Use the service connector pigtail intended for the affected restraint component, following its restraint-service procedure.

diagnostics.finding: A wire moves because its terminal is not retained.
diagnostics.meaning: The terminal may have been making only intermittent contact behind the seal.
diagnostics.next: Identify the correct connector and restore retention through the appropriate service procedure.

diagnostics.finding: A correct mating terminal has very low separation force.
diagnostics.meaning: The contact fit is damaged or loose, provided that housing or retainer drag has not distorted the check.
diagnostics.next: Use the exact connector repair route; do not bend or enlarge contacts as an improvised repair.

diagnostics.finding: A solder-coated strand pierces neighboring insulation.
diagnostics.meaning: The harness can short internally even when its outer wrap looks intact.
diagnostics.next: Use the circuit information to identify both affected conductors and the appropriate repair method.

verification.title: Verify mechanical retention and contact fit
verification.body: Recheck the repaired terminal’s seating, the connector lock and the correct mating contact fit using the same methods that exposed the defect.

verification.title: Return to the circuit diagnosis
verification.body: Repeat the applicable electrical check for the original symptom. A connector that now locks correctly does not by itself establish that every fault in the circuit has been corrected.

notes: Connector-family tool depths are different; use the exact drawing in Wire Terminal Inspection and Removal rather than a depth borrowed from another connector.

guides.title: Plan and seal a soldered wire splice
guides.summary: Choose the correct illustrated solder splice, preserve the circuit-to-pin mapping and seal the finished joint with adhesive-lined heat shrink.
guides.introduction: A soldered splice restores electrical continuity, but the wire layout and insulation seal matter as much as the solder itself. The two illustrated methods use different stripped-wire geometry; the second folds one conductor back after the joint has cooled. They are separate methods, not consecutive halves of one repair.
guides.why: Reversing circuits, using the wrong solder or leaving an air gap at a heat-shrink end can turn a local wiring repair into another fault. Working on one circuit at a time and sealing both ends preserves both the electrical connection and its insulation.

when.summary: When a diagnosed non-restraint wiring defect calls for one of the specified solder-splice methods.
notes: The illustrated methods are limited to 14 AWG and physically smaller-diameter wire; larger AWG numbers denote smaller wire. They do not authorize solder repair of every type of vehicle wiring.

prepare.title: Confirm that this circuit can use the method
prepare.detail: Airbag and seat-belt pretensioner terminals are outside individual-terminal repair: do not remove, repair or replace their individual pins. Use the service connector pigtail intended for the affected restraint component, following its restraint-service procedure. Identify any additional circuit-specific repair restriction before cutting.

prepare.title: Prepare the correct solder and seal
prepare.detail: Use mildly activated rosin-core (RMA) solder, never acid-core solder. The illustrations specify Motorcraft WT-56815 heat shrink for 14–16 AWG and WT-56814 for 18–22 AWG, plus a shielded heat gun.

prepare.title: Keep the complete illustrated method open
prepare.detail: Choose method 1 or method 2 before stripping. Follow that method’s wire layout and heat-shrink overlaps; method 2 deliberately uses unequal stripped lengths and a fold-back arrangement.

steps.title: Isolate power and preserve the pin mapping
steps.body: Disconnect the battery ground cable using the linked battery procedure. Cut and splice one circuit at a time, noting the original wire-to-connector-pin positions before separating anything.

steps.title: Prepare the selected joint geometry
steps.body: Strip the conductors to the layout shown for the selected method and slide on the heat-shrink tube before joining them. Method 1 uses the first drawing’s overlap; method 2 gives wire 1 the longer stripped section needed for the later fold-back.

steps.title: Twist and solder the conductors
steps.body: Twist the wires together in the chosen layout and solder them with RMA rosin-core solder. Do not substitute acid-core solder.

steps.title: Complete the method-specific shape
steps.body: For method 2, let the solder cool before moving the wires, then bend wire 1 back into a straight line as illustrated. Keep method 1 in its own illustrated layout; do not add the second method’s fold-back to it.

steps.title: Seal the joint at both ends
steps.body: Center the heat-shrink tube over the repair so it overlaps insulation on both wires. Heat it with the shielded heat gun until adhesive flows from both ends. On smaller wires, gently squeeze the warm tube ends with pliers as directed to close air gaps.

steps.title: Restore the battery connection
steps.body: Reconnect the battery ground cable through the battery connection procedure after completing the splice and seal.

watchFor.title: Mixing the two layouts
watchFor.body: The longer exposed conductor and fold-back belong to method 2. Using its shape with method 1’s preparation can leave a different joint from either illustrated method.

watchFor.title: Missing heat-shrink overlap
watchFor.body: The tube must cover the repaired area and overlap insulated wire on both sides; adhesive must emerge at both ends.

watchFor.title: Repairing the wrong circuit or component
watchFor.body: One-circuit-at-a-time work preserves the original pin mapping. Restraint terminals require their specified service pigtail, not individual-pin repair.

verification.title: Inspect the completed seal
verification.body: Confirm tube overlap on both insulated conductors, adhesive at both ends and no remaining end gaps. On method 2, confirm that the joint was allowed to cool before the fold-back.

verification.title: Verify the original electrical concern
verification.body: After restoring power, use the applicable circuit check to confirm that the original fault has been addressed.

notes: The linked drawings remain the dimensional reference for each joint. They also show the tube lengths and overlap positions; this overview is not a substitute cut-length template.

guides.title: Select and make a sealed crimp splice
guides.summary: Match the wire gauges, splice and specified crimping tool, then seal the joint using the illustrated method and mixed-gauge matrix.
guides.introduction: A butt splice joins the stripped ends of two conductors inside a crimped barrel. The barrel, wire size and crimping chamber must match. The two crimp-method sheets form one continuous procedure, while the separate matrix determines which combinations are permitted when a service pigtail and the vehicle wire have different gauges.
guides.why: A splice that accepts a wire physically is not necessarily an approved combination. An incorrect barrel or die can leave poor contact, and damaged strands or an incomplete heat-shrink seal can compromise an otherwise sound-looking repair.

when.summary: When a diagnosed wiring repair calls for the specified crimp splice or a permitted mixed-gauge pigtail connection.
notes: The illustrated like-wire procedure covers 8–22 AWG. For unlike wire sizes, the separate repair-kit/vehicle-wire matrix controls whether that combination is allowed.

prepare.title: Check circuit restrictions first
prepare.detail: Airbag and seat-belt pretensioner terminals are outside individual-terminal repair: do not remove, repair or replace their individual pins. Use the service connector pigtail intended for the affected restraint component, following its restraint-service procedure. Confirm that the circuit-specific instructions permit the proposed splice.

prepare.title: Match the splice to the wire and tool
prepare.detail: Use the specified splice and Rotunda NAIAT-R5903 Pro-Crimper; the procedure identifies this as the only tool for those splices. Match the die’s wire-size marking to the marking on the butt splice.

prepare.title: Prepare the correct sealing tube
prepare.detail: The specified Motorcraft heat-shrink tubes are WT-56869 for 8 AWG, WT-56816 for 10–12 AWG, WT-56815 for 14–16 AWG and WT-56814 for 18–22 AWG. Have a shielded heat gun available.

steps.title: Resolve the wire-size combination before cutting
steps.body: For like wire sizes, follow the illustrated 8–22 AWG method. For a different-gauge pigtail, locate the repair-kit size row and vehicle-wire-size column in the matrix and follow that exact cell. A “Not Allowed” cell prohibits that combination; “Solder Only” does not authorize crimping.

steps.title: Isolate and prepare one circuit
steps.body: Disconnect the battery ground cable through the linked procedure. Work on one circuit at a time and preserve its original connector-pin position. Strip 6.35 mm (1/4 in) from each conductor for the illustrated crimp method without nicking or cutting strands, and slide on the heat shrink before assembling the splice.

steps.title: Set up the correct crimping chamber
steps.body: Select the appropriate splice, match its marked wire size to the Pro-Crimper die, and center one end of the barrel in that chamber as illustrated.

steps.title: Crimp both ends
steps.body: Insert the stripped conductor into the barrel and hold it in position while squeezing the tool until the ratchet releases. Repeat the same selection, placement and crimping process for the other end. The continuation sheet recommends applying solder at the barrel ends.

steps.title: Seal the repaired area
steps.body: Center the supplied heat shrink over the completed repair. Apply heat with the shielded heat gun until adhesive flows from both ends of the tube.

steps.title: Restore the connection and test the circuit
steps.body: Reconnect the battery ground cable through the linked procedure. Inspect the finished joint and return to the circuit’s diagnostic check to verify the original concern.

watchFor.title: A kit that does not match the vehicle wire
watchFor.body: Read both matrix axes: repair-kit wire size and vehicle harness wire size are different inputs. Do not treat a nearby permitted cell as approval for the actual pair.

watchFor.title: Cutting conductor strands
watchFor.body: The like-wire method requires stripping without strand damage. The mixed-gauge sheet permits a much narrower exception: when necessary to fit a larger pigtail into the barrel beside a smaller vehicle wire, only pigtail strands equivalent to one wire-size difference may be removed. This is not permission to trim the vehicle harness conductor or remove arbitrary amounts.

watchFor.title: An incomplete crimp or seal
watchFor.body: Use the specified tool and complete its ratchet cycle. Heat-shrink adhesive must emerge at both ends; merely shrinking the tube is not the stated completion criterion.

diagnostics.finding: The chosen matrix cell says “Not Allowed.”
diagnostics.meaning: That repair-kit and vehicle-wire combination is not approved by the matrix.
diagnostics.next: Select a permitted repair method and compatible service parts rather than forcing the wire into the available barrel.

diagnostics.finding: The matrix cell says “Solder Only.”
diagnostics.meaning: The listed combination requires solder instead of the crimp method.
diagnostics.next: Use the applicable illustrated solder method and observe its wire-size and circuit restrictions.

verification.title: Confirm the selected combination
verification.body: Check the finished repair against the same wire sizes, kit row and vehicle-wire column used before work began.

verification.title: Inspect completion before restoring service
verification.body: Confirm that each crimp completed the prescribed ratchet operation, the heat shrink covers the repair and adhesive has flowed from both ends. Then verify the original electrical symptom through its applicable diagnostic procedure.

notes: Sheets 7 and 8 are consecutive parts of the crimp procedure, not alternative methods. Keep both open so preparation, crimping and sealing are considered together.
Use the displayed mixed-gauge matrix directly. Its cell positions carry the meaning; a flattened list of its numbers and “Not Allowed” labels does not.

guides.title: Read a component test: terminals, continuity and sensible conclusions
guides.summary: Learn how to test an isolated switch or relay without confusing a good contact reading with a healthy vehicle circuit.
guides.introduction: A switch is a small traffic controller for electricity: moving it connects or separates particular terminals. A component test checks that internal behavior directly. The schematic explains the electrical relationship, the terminal view identifies the connections, and the test table tells you what should happen in each position.
guides.why: Testing the isolated part keeps the rest of the wiring from creating an alternative path through the meter. Matching the connector and control position matters just as much as taking a reading. Two similar-looking switches can have different internal connections.

applicability.equipment: Only the isolated switches and relays covered by their matching component-test instructions.

procedures.purpose: Identify terminals, isolate the component and read the test correctly.

authoring.method: Codex diagram review and original explanation

when.summary: When a circuit diagnosis calls for checking a switch or relay itself.
notes: These are condition-based checks, not scheduled replacement items.

prepare.title: Isolate the part
prepare.detail: Disconnect the component from the vehicle harness before resistance or continuity testing. Probe the component terminals, not a live harness. Use appropriate leads that contact the terminals without spreading or damaging them.

prepare.title: Understand the meter reading
prepare.detail: A closed circuit means the selected contacts provide an electrical path. An open circuit means they do not. Follow the expected state for the selected position; neither result is automatically a fault.

prepare.title: Choose the exact test
prepare.detail: Have the matching schematic, terminal view and test table open. An ohmmeter or the specified self-powered continuity tester is needed for an unpowered contact test.

steps.title: Identify the component and its connector
steps.body: Start with the fitted part and connector identifier. Distinguish the component face from the mating harness face, and use the shown orientation and molded terminal identifiers. If the drawing, terminal markings or connector shape do not match, resolve the identity before probing.

steps.title: Disconnect the component
steps.body: Separate its electrical connector before a resistance or continuity check. This makes the reading about the selected component rather than everything connected to the vehicle wiring.

steps.title: Choose the circuit and position together
steps.body: Read one complete row: circuit, terminal pair, control position and expected result. Connect the tester to that pair, then move the control to the required position. A reading taken with the control in another position cannot answer that row’s question.

steps.title: Work through the required rows
steps.body: A complaint affecting one function can begin with that circuit. To evaluate the whole component, complete every applicable test row. Record open or closed as specified rather than inventing a universal resistance limit.

steps.title: Separate unpowered and powered tests
steps.body: Relay checks can include a later powered stage. Remove the ohmmeter before applying external power, and follow the exact relay-specific polarity and voltage-test instructions. A switch continuity test does not authorize applying battery power to it.

steps.title: Use the result to choose the next check
steps.body: A repeatable incorrect contact state, with the correct component and sound test connections, points to an internal problem. A correct result only establishes the functions actually tested; wiring, supply, grounds, control modules and driven components still belong to the wider circuit diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: The connector or terminal numbering does not match.
diagnostics.meaning: The selected test may not apply to the fitted part.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the exact equipment and component identity before connecting the tester.

diagnostics.finding: Every applicable row gives the expected state.
diagnostics.meaning: The tested internal connections behave correctly.
diagnostics.next: Continue the vehicle circuit diagnosis if the original symptom remains.

diagnostics.finding: A reading changes when a test lead moves.
diagnostics.meaning: The test connection may be unstable.
diagnostics.next: Secure the leads without damaging the terminal and repeat the same row.

verification.title: Record the complete result
verification.body: Write down the exact component, connector, terminal pair, control position and result. A single successful contact test does not establish that every function works.

verification.title: Finish with the vehicle function
verification.body: Remove the test leads, reconnect the component securely and check the original complaint. If it remains, continue the relevant system diagnosis instead of treating the component check as proof that the entire circuit is healthy.

notes: Use these instructions only for the named component tests. They do not authorize testing airbag or pretensioner terminals.

guides.title: Test the passenger window switch before blaming the motor
guides.summary: Check the passenger switch’s up, down, rest and one-touch contacts with the switch disconnected.
guides.introduction: The passenger window switch sends different requests depending on how far and in which direction you move it. Its ordinary up and down contacts are distinct from the one-touch position. Checking those states helps separate a bad switch contact from a problem elsewhere in the window system.
guides.why: A window that will not move is a symptom, not a switch diagnosis. A disconnected switch check tells you whether its internal contacts make the required connections; it does not test the motor, power supply, wiring or window initialization.

applicability.equipment: Passenger door window switch with connector C624 and the matching up/down and one-touch contact arrangement.

when.summary: When window diagnosis points to the passenger switch or a particular switch position.

prepare.title: Isolate the part
prepare.detail: Disconnect the component from the vehicle harness before resistance or continuity testing. Probe the component terminals, not a live harness. Use appropriate leads that contact the terminals without spreading or damaging them.

prepare.title: Understand the meter reading
prepare.detail: A closed circuit means the selected contacts provide an electrical path. An open circuit means they do not. Follow the expected state for the selected position; neither result is automatically a fault.

prepare.title: Access the switch carefully
prepare.detail: Use the linked front-door switch procedure to release the switch/bezel and disconnect its connector. Passenger and driver switches have different retaining details; this test is for the passenger C624 switch.

steps.title: Confirm the passenger switch
steps.body: Identify C624 and the component-side terminal orientation using the [passenger switch test](#/document/wiring-149-005). The driver’s master control is a different component and must not inherit these connections.

steps.title: Remove vehicle power from the test
steps.body: Disconnect the switch from the harness. This entire contact test is performed without external voltage applied. Leave illumination connections outside the contact test.

steps.title: Check each switch position
steps.body:
Connect an ohmmeter or the specified self-powered tester to the listed pair. Test the rest position as well as both operating directions; contacts that stay closed can be just as significant as contacts that never close.

| Switch position | Terminals to check | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Up | 1 and 2 | Closed |
| Down | 1 and 3 | Closed |
| Rest | 1 and 2; 1 and 3; 2 and 3 | Each pair open |
| One-touch up or down | 1, 2 and 3 | Continuity between these terminals |

steps.title: Recheck an unexpected result
steps.body: Confirm the selected position, component identification and probe contact, then repeat that same test. Do not change the expected result to make an intermittent contact look normal.

steps.title: Choose repair or further diagnosis
steps.body: If a correctly identified switch repeatedly fails its contact test, use the [switch removal and installation](#/document/G1695936) instructions for the repair. If it passes, use [window-system diagnosis](#/document/G1958066) to investigate the remaining complaint.

steps.title: Reconnect and try the original function
steps.body: Secure the connector and switch assembly, then verify ordinary operation and the affected one-touch function as applicable. A switch that passes on the bench has not by itself proved that the complete window system works.

diagnostics.finding: The switch gives the expected contact states.
diagnostics.meaning: The tested switch requests are being made internally.
diagnostics.next: Continue window-system diagnosis if the window still does not respond.

diagnostics.finding: A rest-position pair remains closed.
diagnostics.meaning: The contact behavior does not match the required resting state.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the switch is fully released and the test connection is correct, then repeat.

diagnostics.finding: Ordinary operation passes but one-touch does not.
diagnostics.meaning: The extra switch position needs its own check.
diagnostics.next: Test the one-touch contact state before deciding whether the remaining issue is elsewhere in the system.

verification.title: Record the complete result
verification.body: Write down the exact component, connector, terminal pair, control position and result. A single successful contact test does not establish that every function works.

verification.title: Finish with the vehicle function
verification.body: Remove the test leads, reconnect the component securely and check the original complaint. If it remains, continue the relevant system diagnosis instead of treating the component check as proof that the entire circuit is healthy.

notes: The contact test does not include powering the motor or bridging the vehicle’s harness terminals.

guides.title: Test Micro, Ultra Micro and Power ISO relays
guides.summary: Check a relay’s coil, isolated contacts and powered changeover using the correct test for its relay family.
guides.introduction: A relay uses a small electrical coil to move a separate set of contacts. That lets a control circuit switch another electrical path. A click tells you the mechanism moved; the electrical checks establish whether the coil and contacts actually meet the required conditions.
guides.why: Relay families are not interchangeable test subjects. Their coil-resistance ranges differ, and the Micro ISO powered test uses different coil polarity from the Ultra Micro and Power ISO tests. Identifying the relay first prevents a plausible-looking test from answering the wrong question.

applicability.equipment: Only the matching Micro ISO, Ultra Micro ISO or Power ISO relay shown in the linked component tests; test the removed relay.

when.summary: When circuit diagnosis calls for checking one of these relay types.

prepare.title: Identify the relay and test setup
prepare.detail: Remove the relay from the vehicle circuit and match its terminal layout to the exact relay-family diagram. Have an ohmmeter, voltmeter, suitable test leads and a controlled 12 V DC test supply. Do not bridge vehicle relay-socket terminals as a substitute for this bench test.

prepare.title: Keep resistance and powered tests separate
prepare.detail: Disconnect the ohmmeter before applying voltage. Set up the powered circuit with the supply off and follow the polarity for the identified relay family.

steps.title: Match the relay family and terminal face
steps.body: Open the [Micro ISO](#/document/wiring-149-009), [Ultra Micro ISO](#/document/wiring-149-010) or [Power ISO](#/document/wiring-149-011) test. Match the physical terminal orientation before using the numbers below; do not assign familiar generic relay numbers to this diagram.

steps.title: Measure the unpowered coil and contacts
steps.body:
With no external voltage applied, check every applicable row for that family. The coil should be within its stated resistance range, and the coil must remain electrically isolated from the listed contact terminals.

| Relay family | Coil pair | Coil resistance | Contact check | Coil-to-contact check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Micro ISO | 1–2 | 66–106 ohms | 3–4 closed; 3–5 open | 1–3, 1–4 and 1–5 open |
| Ultra Micro ISO | 1–2 | 87–216 ohms | 3–5 open | 2–3 and 2–5 open |
| Power ISO | 1–2 | 51–125 ohms | 3–5 open | 2–3 and 2–5 open |

steps.title: Prepare for the powered check
steps.body: Remove the ohmmeter completely. Use voltage measurement for the next stage. Confirm the terminal identity again before connecting the test supply; the Micro coil’s ground terminal differs from the other two families.

steps.title: Run the Micro ISO changeover test
steps.body: For Micro ISO only, connect terminals 2 and 3 to 12 V DC and terminal 1 to ground. Measure between 5 and 1: the required result is 12 V. Then remove power from terminal 2 while keeping terminal 3 supplied. Measure between 4 and 1: the required result is again 12 V. Both stages are needed to check the changeover.

steps.title: Run the Ultra Micro or Power ISO test
steps.body: For Ultra Micro ISO or Power ISO only, connect terminals 3 and 1 to 12 V DC and terminal 2 to ground. Measure between 5 and 2: the required result is 12 V. Do not reuse the Micro ISO polarity for these relays.

steps.title: Decide from the electrical result
steps.body: A failed specified check calls for relay replacement after confirming the test setup. If the relay passes but the vehicle fault remains, continue diagnosis of its supply, control and load circuits. Remove the external supply and leads before refitting or replacing the relay.

diagnostics.finding: The relay clicks, but the required output voltage is absent.
diagnostics.meaning: Mechanical movement alone has not established a working contact path.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the exact family, supply and probe connections; repeat its powered test.

diagnostics.finding: The coil resistance is outside the range for that family.
diagnostics.meaning: The coil does not meet that relay’s specified check.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the relay identity and meter connection, then replace a confirmed failed relay.

diagnostics.finding: The relay passes every specified stage.
diagnostics.meaning: Its tested bench behavior is correct.
diagnostics.next: Continue the vehicle circuit diagnosis instead of assuming the entire system is healthy.

verification.title: Keep results by relay family
verification.body: Record the relay identity, coil resistance, unpowered contact states and powered voltage results. For Micro ISO, retain both changeover-stage results.

verification.title: Finish with the vehicle function
verification.body: Remove the test leads, reconnect the component securely and check the original complaint. If it remains, continue the relevant system diagnosis instead of treating the component check as proof that the entire circuit is healthy.

notes: These terminal assignments are specific to the illustrated relays. A similar housing or a familiar clicking sound does not establish an identical internal circuit.

guides.title: Test door-lock and memory buttons by their contact states
guides.summary: Check left, right and memory-equipped door switches without confusing their different common terminals.
guides.introduction: A door-lock switch makes a small electrical request when you press lock or unlock. A memory-equipped left switch adds separate seat-memory requests. The test checks those button contacts inside the disconnected switch; it does not drive a door latch or prove that a memory seat can move.
guides.why: Left, right and memory-equipped switches use different connector and terminal assignments. Keeping each variant separate prevents a good switch from failing a test that belongs to another door. Checking the released position also reveals a contact that remains closed after the button is let go.

applicability.equipment: C505 left door switch without memory, C541 left door switch with memory, or C605 right door switch, as fitted.

prepare.title: Choose the correct variant
prepare.detail: Identify the door side and whether memory buttons are fitted. Match C505, C541 or C605 before selecting a terminal pair.

steps.title: Identify the switch and disconnect it
steps.body: Use the [left switch without memory](#/document/wiring-149-006), [left switch with memory](#/document/wiring-149-007) or [right switch](#/document/wiring-149-008) test. Disconnect the component from the harness before using the meter.

steps.title: Test lock and unlock separately
steps.body:
For each listed pair, check all three button states. “Rest” means no button is pressed.

| Switch | Pair | Rest | Lock | Unlock |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C505 left, no memory | 3 and 2 | Open | Open | Closed |
| C505 left, no memory | 4 and 3 | Open | Closed | Open |
| C541 left, memory | 1 and 3 | Open | Open | Closed |
| C541 left, memory | 2 and 3 | Open | Closed | Open |
| C605 right | 3 and 2 | Open | Open | Closed |
| C605 right | 1 and 2 | Open | Closed | Open |

steps.title: Check memory buttons only where fitted
steps.body: On C541, test 5 and 3 for Set 1, 6 and 3 for Set 2, and 7 and 3 for Set 3. Each pair must be open with its button released and closed while that corresponding Set button is pressed. These checks evaluate the buttons, not stored seat positions or the seat module.

steps.title: Repeat a questionable contact result
steps.body: Confirm the correct switch, terminal orientation and probe contact. Press and release the same button again and compare with the required states. Do not judge all of the switch’s functions from one successful button.

steps.title: Return to the system complaint
steps.body: Reconnect securely after testing. If the contacts pass but locking still fails, continue [locks and entry-system diagnosis](#/document/G1695898). A working request switch does not rule out a latch, supply, wiring or control problem.

diagnostics.finding: Lock works but unlock fails the contact check.
diagnostics.meaning: The two requests use distinct contact paths.
diagnostics.next: Verify the unlock pair for that exact switch and repeat the test.

diagnostics.finding: A memory button closes correctly, but the seat does not respond.
diagnostics.meaning: The button-contact test has passed; the seat system has not been tested.
diagnostics.next: Continue diagnosis of the fitted memory-seat system.

diagnostics.finding: A pair remains closed with the button released.
diagnostics.meaning: Its resting state is incorrect for this test.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the control has returned to rest and repeat with sound test connections.

verification.title: Record the complete result
verification.body: Write down the exact component, connector, terminal pair, control position and result. A single successful contact test does not establish that every function works.

verification.title: Finish with the vehicle function
verification.body: Remove the test leads, reconnect the component securely and check the original complaint. If it remains, continue the relevant system diagnosis instead of treating the component check as proof that the entire circuit is healthy.

notes: No external power is applied during these contact checks.

guides.title: Test the headlamp switch’s lighting requests
guides.summary: Check the disconnected lighting switch’s headlamp, parking, auto, dimmer and applicable fog-button contacts.
guides.introduction: The lighting switch tells the car which lighting mode you want. Its internal contact positions are requests, so a particular switch contact being open does not necessarily mean the corresponding lamps should be dark. This check looks at the switch itself, separately from the rest of the lighting system.
guides.why: The normal knob positions deliberately connect different terminals. Testing them as a matrix is more useful than assuming every lamp-related contact must stay closed whenever any exterior light is on. The Auto position also needs a distinct check from the ordinary On position.

applicability.equipment: Headlamp switch C205 with the matching listed functions; test rear-fog controls only if fitted.

prepare.title: Protect the dash trim
prepare.detail: Use the linked access procedure and a non-marring trim tool. Release the retaining tabs and electrical connector as instructed rather than pulling the switch out by its wiring.

steps.title: Access and isolate C205
steps.body: Use [headlamp switch removal](#/document/G1694120) and match the [component test](#/document/wiring-149-012). Disconnect the switch connector before testing, and identify the component-side terminal orientation.

steps.title: Check all knob positions
steps.body:
For each pair, move through Off, Park, On and Auto. Each row describes an internal request contact, not a measurement at the exterior lamps.

| Terminal pair | Off | Park | On | Auto |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 and 12 — headlamp request | Open | Open | Closed | Open |
| 4 and 13 — auto request | Open | Open | Open | Closed |
| 4 and 11 — parking request | Open | Closed | Open | Open |
| 4 and 10 — off request | Closed | Open | Open | Open |

steps.title: Test the separate buttons where fitted
steps.body: Check 4 and 6 for Dim +, and 4 and 3 for Dim −. Each is open with its button off and closed when that button is operated. If rear-fog control is fitted, 4 and 2 is open with that control off and closed with rear fog selected. Do not invent a front-fog or headlamp-leveling test from the schematic alone.

steps.title: Repeat the exact failed condition
steps.body: Confirm the chosen knob or button state and terminal pair before deciding the switch is faulty. A poor probe connection can imitate an open contact. Record the specific function that does not match.

steps.title: Reassemble and check the complaint
steps.body: Follow the switch installation sequence, reconnecting and securing its trim. Verify the affected lighting operation. If the switch passes but the lamps still behave incorrectly, continue the appropriate lighting-circuit diagnosis instead of treating the contact test as a whole-system result.

diagnostics.finding: The Auto contact passes, but automatic lighting still misbehaves.
diagnostics.meaning: The switch is making its tested Auto request.
diagnostics.next: Continue the lighting-system diagnosis; this test does not evaluate the remaining control inputs.

diagnostics.finding: A dimmer button does not produce the expected closed state.
diagnostics.meaning: That button’s contact path has not passed.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the terminal pair and repeat the operated and released states.

diagnostics.finding: A contact is open in a position where the table requires open.
diagnostics.meaning: That is the expected internal switch state.
diagnostics.next: Judge it against the complete matrix, not whether an exterior lamp happens to be on.

verification.title: Record the complete result
verification.body: Write down the exact component, connector, terminal pair, control position and result. A single successful contact test does not establish that every function works.

verification.title: Finish with the vehicle function
verification.body: Remove the test leads, reconnect the component securely and check the original complaint. If it remains, continue the relevant system diagnosis instead of treating the component check as proof that the entire circuit is healthy.

notes: Only the listed contact tests are included. Illumination electronics and additional market-dependent controls are not established by these readings.

guides.summary: Check the electrical paths for seat travel, height, tilt and the applicable left-seat lumbar control.
guides.introduction: The seat switch selects an electrical path for each direction of movement. Forward and rearward, for example, use different contact combinations. Testing the disconnected switch can identify a contact problem without assuming that an unresponsive seat must have a failed motor.

applicability.equipment: Matching left six-way or eight-way power-seat switch C352, or right six-way power-seat switch C3190. Excludes manual-seat controls.

prepare.title: Establish terminal identity before probing
prepare.detail: Use the fitted switch’s reliable terminal identifiers and matching connector information. The required test terminals include 9 and 10. Do not infer their locations from an eight-cavity picture or count positions on a different switch. If terminal identity cannot be established, obtain the correct component identification before testing.

prepare.title: Use controlled switch access
prepare.detail: Follow the front-seat switch access procedure for the recline handle, side shield, knob and switch retainers. Keep the test confined to the seat control switch; do not probe nearby restraint connectors.

steps.body: Identify left C352 or right C3190 and the fitted functions. Open the [left six-way](#/document/wiring-149-002), [left eight-way](#/document/wiring-149-003) or [right six-way](#/document/wiring-149-004) test. The table below gives terminal identities, not physical probe locations.

steps.title: Access the isolated switch
steps.body: Follow [seat-switch access](#/document/G1695513), disconnecting the switch electrical connector. Check the component’s terminal identity before attaching an ohmmeter or the specified self-powered tester. The [C352](#/document/connector-C352) and [C3190](#/document/connector-C3190) assignments help identify the electrical functions; connector shape and orientation still must match the fitted part.

steps.title: Check both paths for each movement
steps.body:
Hold the selected movement while testing each listed pair separately. Every pair shown must read closed in that operating position.

| Movement | Left C352 pairs | Right C3190 pairs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Forward | 9–5 and 7–6 | 8–2 and 10–1 |
| Rearward | 9–6 and 7–5 | 8–1 and 10–2 |
| Height up | 9–8 and 7–10 | 8–9 and 10–7 |
| Height down | 9–10 and 7–8 | 8–7 and 10–9 |
| Tilt up | 9–1 and 7–2 | 8–6 and 10–5 |
| Tilt down | 9–2 and 7–1 | 8–5 and 10–6 |

steps.title: Add the left eight-way lumbar checks
steps.body: For the applicable left eight-way switch only, the position labeled Inflate requires closed paths at 9–4 and 7–3. The position labeled Deflate requires closed paths at 9–3 and 7–4. Treat these as switch-position labels; this contact test does not establish the health of the complete lumbar mechanism.

steps.title: Interpret the failed direction
steps.body: If a movement fails, repeat both of its contact checks with sound probe connections and confirmed terminal identity. A pass establishes those switch contacts only. It does not test motor load, seat-track movement, the vehicle power feed or the seat’s other controls.

steps.title: Restore the switch and check operation
steps.body: Remove the leads and reinstall the switch, knob, side shield and handle using the access procedure. Reconnect securely and verify the original movement complaint. Continue the seat-system diagnosis if a correctly functioning switch does not resolve the symptom.

diagnostics.finding: One of a movement’s two pairs remains open.
diagnostics.meaning: That movement has not passed its complete switch-contact check.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the pair and switch position, then repeat both paths.

diagnostics.finding: The required terminals cannot be identified reliably.
diagnostics.meaning: The component identity or connector geometry is unresolved.
diagnostics.next: Stop probing and establish the correct fitted-switch terminal identification.

diagnostics.finding: All tested contacts pass but the seat remains stationary.
diagnostics.meaning: The switch test has not found the cause in those contacts.
diagnostics.next: Continue diagnosis of the fitted seat system, its supply, wiring and driven mechanism.

verification.title: Record the complete result
verification.body: Write down the exact component, connector, terminal pair, control position and result. A single successful contact test does not establish that every function works.

verification.title: Finish with the vehicle function
verification.body: Remove the test leads, reconnect the component securely and check the original complaint. If it remains, continue the relevant system diagnosis instead of treating the component check as proof that the entire circuit is healthy.

guides.title: Overhaul the 6R80 six-speed automatic transmission
guides.summary: Remove the transmission, inspect and rebuild its hydraulic and mechanical assemblies, set the required clearances, then reinstall and complete calibration and fluid checks.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 passes engine power through a torque converter into planetary gears. Electronically controlled hydraulic pressure applies internal clutches to select the gears. Overhaul means complete dismantling, cleaning, inspection, seal renewal and measured reassembly—not simply replacing the clutch plates. The bench procedure serves the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications, but vehicle access, clutch quantities and some internal parts differ.
guides.why: Debris remaining in the converter or cooling circuit can damage rebuilt components. Incorrect clutch clearance, misplaced bearings or mismatched parts can prevent proper operation even when everything looks clean. Electronic calibration also matters: the transmission controller must use the strategy matching the installed solenoid body.

when.summary: When diagnosis and inspection establish internal wear or damage requiring complete transmission rebuilding.
notes: Harsh shifts alone do not establish that an overhaul is needed; an incorrect solenoid strategy can also produce them.

prepare.title: Arrange specialist handling and bench equipment
prepare.detail: You need safe hoist access, a high-lift transmission jack with restraint, torque converter retainer and handling tools, transmission holding fixture, press, specified clutch spring compressors, bearing and seal tools, dial indicator and depth gauges. Bench work includes controlled shop-air piston removal.

prepare.title: Have the supporting procedures and capabilities ready
prepare.detail: Use the engine-specific access procedure and its lifting, starter, driveshaft, exhaust and crossmember prerequisites. Arrange converter flushing, cooler backflushing and a diagnostic scan tool capable of the required corrections and learning procedures.

prepare.title: Prepare fluids and replacement parts
prepare.detail: Use the specified Motorcraft MERCON LV automatic transmission fluid and gasket kit -7153-. Renew seals, gaskets and all designated one-use components, including the filter, discarded clutch retainers, direct clutch hub, roll pin and specified fasteners. Select clutch parts for the actual engine.

steps.title: Choose the correct vehicle access route
steps.body: Start with the [removal entry](#/document/G1692037) and the applicable procedure. All variants require starter and driveshaft removal. The [2.3L procedure](#/document/G1692044) includes the starter insulator, catalytic converter bracket, dust shield and cooler-tube supports. The [3.7L procedure](#/document/G1692046) includes the access cover and left catalyst monitor sensor. The [5.0L procedure](#/document/G1692048) additionally removes the right catalytic converter, left heated oxygen and catalyst monitor sensors, and flexplate inspection cover. Follow the fitted shield or shield-and-subframe-bracket branch.

steps.title: Drain, support and remove the transmission
steps.body: Position the vehicle on the hoist in NEUTRAL. Rotate the crankshaft clockwise only, mark a converter stud against the flexplate and discard the converter nuts. Drain through pan removal, then refit the pan. Disconnect the cooler tubes and selector cable as directed. Restrain the jack-supported transmission with contact at the pan's outer ribs before removing the crossmember. Release wiring and bellhousing attachments in engine-specific order; fit the converter retainer before removing the transmission.

steps.title: Clean the cooling circuit and assess the converter
steps.body: Backflush and clean the cooler circuit whenever overhauling or replacing the transmission. Mount the transmission securely on its bench fixture and remove the converter with its handling tool. Converter flushing is mandatory during overhaul. Use the specified heated, pulsating equipment with flow measurement, filtration and air purge. Follow the full setup, flushing and cooling sequence. Hand flushing is permitted only when compliant heated equipment is unavailable and the fluid contains no metallic contamination.

steps.title: Dismantle in the prescribed order
steps.body: The [disassembly procedure](#/document/G1692070) leads to the [complete overhaul sequence](#/document/G1692066). Remove the pan, filter, connector sleeve, main control, feed seals and pump before extracting clutch and planetary assemblies. Keep plate groups together and identify shims, bearings and orientation marks. Unstake the output flange nut before removal and discard it. Continue through the output bearings and parking mechanism; bearing pullers must contact the bearing rather than the case lip.

steps.title: Rebuild the clutch assemblies
steps.body: Inspect the forward, overdrive, direct, intermediate and low/reverse assemblies. Replace excessively worn or damaged plates; serviceable plates may be reused. Renew the specified piston seals, sealing rings and discarded retainers using the designated compressors and seal-sizing tools. Confirm retaining rings are seated before releasing spring pressure. Soak plates in clean transmission fluid and follow each pack's stacking order. Match engine-specific plate quantities and any replacement intermediate piston height.

steps.title: Measure rather than assume clutch clearance
steps.body: For the forward, overdrive, direct and intermediate clutches, record and average the opposed dial-indicator readings. Correct excessive clearance with a thicker selective snap ring, or insufficient clearance with a thinner one. Low/reverse clearance uses case depth minus clutch-pack height and piston-to-support height; adjust its selective plate and remeasure. Use the [specifications](#/document/G1686431) for the applicable quantities and limits.

steps.title: Rebuild the pump and rear transmission
steps.body: Follow the [assembly route](#/document/G1692071) through the overhaul procedure. Inspect pump gears, surfaces and bushings, then assemble with the alignment marks, gear orientation and new seals specified. Restore the parking mechanism with new discarded hardware. Install the output assembly, planetary components, low/reverse plates, one-way clutch and center support in order, preserving bearing and snap-ring orientations. Measure rear end play with the new flange nut loose; select the correct shim before tightening and staking the nut.

steps.title: Complete the front assembly and hydraulic controls
steps.body: Install the remaining clutch assemblies, selective shim and pump with new pump-to-case bolts and washers. Measure input end play; remove the pump and change the shim if necessary. Renew feed-tube and pump-adapter seals, inspect the thermal bypass valve and align the main control's manual valve with its linkage. Follow the illustrated tightening sequence. Fully seat and lock the connector sleeve, install a new filter, close the pan and install the converter.

steps.title: Refill and reinstall through the correct engine procedure
steps.body: Use the [installation entry](#/document/G1692042) to return to the appropriate engine procedure. Record the strategy identification before fitting a new transmission or a rebuilt unit with a new main control; replace the tag when required. Follow the prefill branch, grease the converter pilot and keep the converter fully seated while aligning the transmission on the engine dowels. Restore attachments with new converter nuts and cooler-tube bolt. Inspect and lubricate cooler seals and backing rings, replacing damaged parts.

steps.title: Restore adjustment and electronic setup
steps.body: Verify selector-cable adjustment and perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction with the scan tool. Download the solenoid strategy if the transmission or main control was replaced. Complete the adaptive learning drive cycle after overhaul, then perform the warm-circulation and final fluid-level checks below.

watchFor.title: Converter flushing hazards
watchFor.body: Watch the converter throughout heated flushing and stop immediately if a leak develops. The converter, adapter and hoses become hot; allow the specified 30-minute cooling period before handling. Never flush the converter with water-based cleaners or mineral spirits.

watchFor.title: Small assembly details with major consequences
watchFor.body: Position the new direct-clutch-hub retaining-ring gap approximately 120° from its original marked location. Hook the pump seal-ring ends together. Do not pull on the wiring harness to disconnect the transmission connector.

notes: The pan gasket is specifically reusable if undamaged.

Use only 9–10 ml of XL-16 additive F after complete fluid replacement or replacement of the overdrive friction plates. Do not use the kit's tracer T syringe; excess additive can cause converter-clutch slip. Supplemental additives and cleaning agents are not permitted during converter flushing.

diagnostics.finding: Converter seal-track groove, damaged studs, threaded pads, hub or bushing, overheating discoloration, water/antifreeze contamination, or diagnostically confirmed malfunction.
diagnostics.meaning: The converter meets a replacement criterion.
diagnostics.next: Install a new or remanufactured converter.

diagnostics.finding: Metallic contamination in the converter-fluid sample.
diagnostics.meaning: Hand flushing is not acceptable.
diagnostics.next: Use the specified heated flushing equipment; do not continue the hand-flushing branch.

diagnostics.finding: Pump wear marks or damaged pump components.
diagnostics.meaning: Light internal scratches can be normal; burned, discolored or scored gears, damaged teeth and damaged bushings require a different decision.
diagnostics.next: Follow the pump inspection criteria and replace the pump where specified, including for damaged input-shaft or converter-hub bushings.

diagnostics.finding: The main-control strategy differs from the scan-tool display.
diagnostics.meaning: Incorrect calibration can cause harsh shifts.
diagnostics.next: Download the matching strategy rather than treating shift feel alone as proof of mechanical failure.

verification.title: Keep the measurement record
verification.body: Retain the clutch readings and calculations, selected adjustment parts, and final rear and input end-play readings. Every clearance must meet its own specification before closing the assembly.

verification.title: Confirm warm circulation and final level
verification.body: During driving, verify transmission fluid temperature reaches 96.7°C–102°C using the scan tool. This circulates fluid through the converter and cooling system to remove trapped air. Then complete the prescribed transmission fluid level check; the installation prefill does not replace it.

guides.title: Replace the accessory-drive idler pulley on the 2.3L EcoBoost
guides.summary: Replace the 2.3L accessory-drive idler, following the separate belt-removal sequence and checking both belts after refitting.
guides.introduction: The idler is the freely rotating pulley that guides and supports the accessory belt along its route. It is separate from the tensioner, which is the component moved to release belt tension. On the 2.3L EcoBoost, reaching the idler means dealing with two belts in the correct sequence: the A/C compressor belt comes off before the main accessory belt.
guides.why: Taking the belt load off first makes the pulley attachment accessible. The central bolt holds the idler in position while the pulley rotates around its bearing. Correct fastening and final belt seating matter together: a securely mounted pulley cannot guide a belt correctly if that belt is sitting outside its intended grooves.

when.summary: When inspection or diagnosis establishes that the 2.3L accessory-drive idler needs replacement.
notes: A belt-drive noise does not by itself identify the idler as the faulty component. Confirm which pulley or belt needs attention before replacing parts.

prepare.title: Plan the two-belt access sequence
prepare.detail: Have the full A/C belt and accessory-belt procedures available. The A/C belt uses its own removal and installation method, including the specified installation aid; it is not released by the main belt tensioner.

prepare.title: Prepare the fastening tools
prepare.detail: Use suitable access tools and a torque wrench capable of 10.5 Nm. Identify the idler’s central bolt in its component illustration before removing it.

steps.title: Remove the separate A/C compressor belt
steps.body: Follow the [2.3L A/C compressor-belt procedure](#/document/G1688221), including its access steps and stretchy-belt-tool method. Keep the separate belt installation instructions with the job so their hand-rotation and seating checks are not missed later.

steps.title: Release the main accessory belt
steps.body: Use the [accessory-drive belt procedure](#/document/G1688219). Rotate its tensioner counter clockwise and remove the belt. The tensioner releases belt tension; the idler is the different pulley being replaced.

steps.title: Remove and refit the idler
steps.body: Remove the central retaining bolt and the idler pulley identified in the [idler illustration](#/document/G2086104). Refit the pulley and its central bolt, tightening the bolt to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm). This value belongs to the idler attachment, not to the tensioner mounting.

steps.title: Restore the belts and verify their seating
steps.body: Complete the linked belt installation sequence. The A/C belt instructions temporarily position the main belt away from the crankshaft pulley, then reinstall it after the A/C belt is fitted. Perform the specified hand-rotation checks, remove the installation aid and confirm that each belt is correctly seated on all of its pulleys.

watchFor.title: Confusing the idler with the tensioner
watchFor.body: The idler’s central fastening value is different from the mounting requirements of the tensioner assembly. Use the component picture to keep their jobs separate.

watchFor.title: A belt sitting outside its grooves
watchFor.body: Inspect the belt path after installation. The required seating checks include both the A/C belt and the main accessory belt.

verification.title: Confirm the idler attachment
verification.body: Confirm the idler’s central bolt has been tightened to its specified value and the pulley is installed in its illustrated position.

verification.title: Complete both belt procedures
verification.body: Confirm the installation aid has been removed, the prescribed hand-rotation checks are complete and both belts are correctly seated.

guides.title: Replace the output shaft seal on the 5.2L 3160 manual transmission
guides.summary: Service the transmission's rear output seal with dedicated installers and inspect the speed-sensor tone wheel before restoring the output flange.
guides.introduction: The output shaft carries transmission torque toward the rear driveshaft through its flange. A seal at the rear housing keeps transmission oil inside around this rotating connection. Replacing that seal requires removing the flange, discarding the old seal and inspecting the nearby speed-sensor tone wheel. This job applies to the 3160 six-speed manual transmission used with the 5.2L engine.
guides.why: The seal and tone wheel have different replacement rules: always renew the removed seal, while replacing the tone wheel only if it is damaged. Fit the tone wheel before installing the seal. The specified installer combination supports and aligns the new seal while it is fitted into the rear housing.

when.summary: When an output-shaft seal repair is required or the seal has been removed during related work.
notes: Confirm the transmission before selecting parts and procedures; its identification tag is on the top right-hand side.

prepare.title: Specified installers and replacement parts
prepare.detail: Have installer 205-199 (T83T-3132-A1), output shaft seal installer 308-959 and a new seal. A replacement tone wheel is needed if inspection finds damage.

prepare.title: Flange-service capability
prepare.detail: Be equipped to complete the exact output-flange removal and installation procedure, including its specified renewed parts and tightening requirements. Keep the seal-installer arrangement and the same-transmission assembly sequence available while reassembling.

steps.title: Remove the output shaft flange
steps.body: Follow the [Transmission Output Shaft Flange procedure](#/document/G1805399) to gain access to the seal. Keep that procedure available for the later flange installation.

steps.title: Remove and discard the seal
steps.body: Remove the output shaft seal and discard it. The replacement requirement applies even if the removed seal appears intact.

steps.title: Inspect the speed-sensor tone wheel
steps.body: Remove the speed-sensor tone wheel and inspect it for damage. Use a new tone wheel if damage is found; otherwise retain the serviceable wheel. Refit the tone wheel before fitting the output seal, as shown in the [same-transmission assembly sequence](#/document/G1849280).

steps.title: Install the new seal with its dedicated tools
steps.body: Place the new seal on the specified combination of 205-199 and 308-959, using the arrangement pictured in the [seal procedure](#/document/G1794237). Use that tool combination to install the seal into the rear housing. Keep the tool aligned with the opening.

steps.title: Restore the output flange
steps.body: With the tone wheel and new seal installed, complete the [output-flange installation](#/document/G1805399). Follow that procedure’s parts-renewal and tightening requirements rather than treating the flange as an ordinary bolt-on cover.

watchFor.title: Reusing the removed seal
watchFor.body: A removed output seal is discarded even if it appears intact. Have the replacement ready before reassembly.

watchFor.title: Omitting the tone wheel
watchFor.body: The tone wheel belongs ahead of the seal in this installation sequence. Record its inspection result and refit the serviceable or replacement wheel before installing the seal.

diagnostics.finding: Damage is found on the removed speed-sensor tone wheel.
diagnostics.meaning: The tone wheel meets the stated replacement condition.
diagnostics.next: Install a new tone wheel as part of the completed reassembly.

verification.title: Record the tone-wheel decision
verification.body: Record whether inspection found damage and whether a replacement was required.

verification.title: Confirm completion of the installation sequence
verification.body: Confirm the tone wheel is refitted, a new seal is installed with the specified tools and the complete output-flange installation has been finished.

guides.title: Replace the coolant degas bottle on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Isolate and empty the degas bottle, disconnect its hoses, replace it and restore the specified coolant mixture and level.
guides.introduction: The degas bottle holds surplus coolant, accommodates expansion, helps remove air and provides the cooling system's service-fill point. It also participates in system pressurization. Replacing it therefore involves more than exchanging a container: its hose connections, pressure cap and final coolant fill all need to be restored correctly.
guides.why: Hot coolant remains hazardous under pressure, and even slightly loosening the cap can release steam and liquid forcefully. Clamping the lower hose before emptying the bottle limits coolant movement through that connection. Selecting the correct engine procedure keeps hose access and component positioning tied to the actual installation.

when.summary: When the degas bottle requires removal or replacement after the cooling concern has been assessed.
notes: Coolant loss or overheating alone does not identify the bottle as the failed component.

prepare.title: Allow the engine to cool
prepare.detail: Do not open the cooling system while the engine is running or the system is hot. The 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures additionally require a thick cloth over the cap while releasing pressure.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified equipment
prepare.detail: Have a fluid suction gun, locking pliers and a hose clamp remover/installer, together with tools for the mounting bolts.

prepare.title: Identify the correct refill
prepare.detail: The procedures specify Motorcraft Orange concentrated coolant VC-3-B, WSS-M97B44-D, or Orange prediluted coolant VC-3DIL-B, WSS-M97B44-D2. Establish the recommended mixture and fill level before emptying the bottle; concentrate and prediluted coolant require different preparation.

steps.title: Select the engine-specific route
steps.body: Use the matching removal and installation procedure: [2.3L](#/document/G1673131), [3.7L](#/document/G1694561), [5.0L](#/document/G1694593) or [5.2L](#/document/G1807375). Their overall sequence is shared, but their illustrations show the relevant hose layout and access.

steps.title: Open the cooled system
steps.body: Once the engine and cooling system have cooled, remove the pressure relief cap. Apply the thick-cloth precaution required for the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L branches.

steps.title: Isolate and empty the bottle
steps.body: Clamp the lower degas-bottle hose using the specified locking pliers, then siphon coolant from the bottle with the fluid suction gun. Emptying it before disconnecting the hoses reduces the coolant remaining in the component being handled.

steps.title: Release the upper connections and mountings
steps.body: Use the hose clamp remover/installer to release the upper-hose clamps and disconnect the hoses. Remove the bottle mounting bolts so it can be repositioned for lower-hose access.

steps.title: Disconnect the lower hose
steps.body: Position the bottle as shown for the selected engine. Release the lower-hose connection with the hose-clamp tool and remove the bottle.

steps.title: Install and refill
steps.body: Reverse removal, reconnecting the lower hose and restoring the bottle mountings and upper connections. Tighten the mounting bolts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Release the temporary lower-hose clamp. Fill with the recommended coolant mixture to the specified level and restore the pressure cap.

watchFor.title: Heat or pressure before opening
watchFor.body: A pressure cap must not be loosened on a running engine or hot system. Allow cooling before proceeding.

watchFor.title: A temporary clamp left installed
watchFor.body: The lower-hose isolation is temporary; reverse that operation when restoring the cooling connections.

notes: Use the illustration for your selected engine to identify the lower-hose connection.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical restoration
verification.body: Check that all disconnected hoses and their clamps are restored, the temporary clamp is removed and the mounting bolts have received the specified torque.

verification.title: Confirm the refill
verification.body: Verify the coolant product, mixture and final fill level against the selected engine's requirements, and confirm the pressure cap is installed.

guides.title: Replace the A/C receiver drier using the correct engine access route
guides.summary: Replace the receiver drier through the engine-specific access route, then restore the refrigerant system's oil balance, vacuum and charge.
guides.introduction: The air-conditioning (A/C) receiver drier helps manage liquid refrigerant and moisture within the refrigerant circuit. Replacing it opens that circuit, so removing the small component is only part of the job. Refrigerant must first be identified and recovered, and the completed system must be evacuated and charged. Access differs significantly: the 2.3L requires condenser removal, while the other listed engines use underbody access.
guides.why: Contamination can enter through an open connection, and contaminated refrigerant can spoil recovery equipment's stored supply. Oil removed during recovery also needs to be accounted for. Correct access, sealing and refrigerant servicing are therefore as important as securing the replacement drier.

when.summary: When receiver-drier replacement has been established as part of a refrigerant-system repair.
notes: Select the procedure by engine before dismantling; the access and seal instructions are not identical.
These replacement procedures do not diagnose poor cooling.

prepare.title: Arrange refrigerant-service capability
prepare.detail: Use refrigerant identification equipment and the Ford-approved R134A management equipment specified in the recovery procedure, following equipment instructions.

prepare.title: Prepare lifting and service materials
prepare.detail: Provide hoist access using the lifting procedure, with the transmission in NEUTRAL. Obtain the applicable charge, oil and seal-lubrication specifications before opening the system.

prepare.title: Plan the required seals
prepare.detail: The 2.3L condenser procedure and the 5.2L drier procedure require new O-ring seals lubricated only with the specified material. Protect exposed openings against contamination.

steps.title: Identify and recover the refrigerant
steps.body: Check purity before recovery. Connect to both high- and low-side service ports; low-side-only recovery is prohibited. Record any oil recovered. After recovery, confirm the vacuum remains stable for about 2 minutes, repeating the recovery sequence if it does not.

steps.title: Follow the correct access branch
steps.body: For the 2.3L, follow the condenser procedure: remove the required shields and intake components, disconnect and cover refrigerant ports, reposition the degas bottle and cooling assembly, then release the condenser. For the 3.7L and 5.0L, remove the underbody shield bolts and retainers. For the 5.2L, complete both specified underbody-shield removal operations.

steps.title: Remove the receiver drier
steps.body: Remove the air deflector, then the drier attachment bolts, retainer and drier. On the 2.3L this follows condenser removal. Keep the engine-specific illustrations and instructions with the work so access details are not transferred between variants.

steps.title: Install and close the system
steps.body: Reverse the applicable removal sequence. The drier attachment bolts are tightened to 80 lb.in (9 Nm) in all four procedures. Fit the required new O-rings for the 2.3L condenser connections and 5.2L drier, using the specified lubricant. Remove temporary port protection when reconnecting.

steps.title: Restore the correct oil quantity
steps.body: Follow Refrigerant Oil Adding for the correct amount of clean polyalkylene glycol (PAG) oil. Account for the oil recovered, which must be replaced, alongside the applicable component-replacement requirements. Do not guess an oil quantity or transfer one between engines.

steps.title: Evacuate and charge
steps.body: Evacuate to at least 99.4 kPa (29.5 in-Hg) of vacuum, as close to 101.1 kPa (30 in-Hg) as possible, and continue pumping for at least 45 minutes. Stop the pump and observe vacuum retention for 10 minutes. Set the correct refrigerant charge amount and charge according to the service-unit instructions.

watchFor.title: Contaminated refrigerant
watchFor.body: Do not recover it into the normal bulk supply. Follow the contamination route, including dedicated contaminated-refrigerant recovery equipment and the specified disposal requirements.

watchFor.title: Misread access illustration
watchFor.body: The 2.3L condenser illustration notes that the bumper is removed for clarity; that note is not an instruction to remove it.

notes: The 3.7L and 5.0L underbody-shield fasteners have their own installation setting; do not use the drier-bolt setting for them.

diagnostics.finding: Vacuum is lost during the post-recovery observation.
diagnostics.meaning: The recovery procedure has not reached its required stable-vacuum condition.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the prescribed recovery sequence until vacuum remains stable for 2 minutes.

verification.title: Confirm evacuation completion
verification.body: Verify the specified evacuation and vacuum-hold stages before completing charging.

verification.title: Record the service result
verification.body: Record recovered oil, oil added, the vacuum-hold result and the refrigerant charge used for the vehicle.
