guides.title: Replace the engine block heater on the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L
guides.summary: Drain the correct cooling system, replace the block heater and restore its protected wiring route before filling and bleeding.
guides.introduction: The block heater uses electrical heat to warm the engine through its coolant. Removing it opens the cooling system, so the repair includes coolant draining and a complete filling and bleeding stage. The 2.3L additionally requires starter motor removal for access; the 3.7L and 5.0L procedures proceed directly to the heater after draining.
guides.why: The heater must be tightened correctly at its coolant connection, and its wiring must remain secured away from hot or rotating components. Correct filling and bleeding restores the cooling circuit after the opening has admitted air. A nearby coolant leak should be located accurately before assuming the heater is responsible.

when.summary: When a block-heater fault has been established or heater removal is required for related repair work.
notes: Select coolant-service instructions by engine, even though the heater tightening specification is shared.

prepare.title: Prepare for coolant service
prepare.detail: Have the matching engine’s draining, vacuum filling and bleeding procedure available, together with its required equipment and coolant specifications. Follow its precautions before opening the cooling system.

prepare.title: Prepare electrical and access work
prepare.detail: Ensure the heater is disconnected from its power supply. For the 2.3L, follow the starter procedure’s preparation requirements before removing the starter; this prerequisite is part of the access work.

steps.title: Drain the matching cooling system
steps.body: Use the coolant procedure for the [2.3L](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L](#/document/G1694549) or [5.0L](#/document/G1694583). Complete draining before disconnecting and removing the heater.

steps.title: Create access on the 2.3L
steps.body: Remove the starter motor using the [2.3L starter procedure](#/document/G1673178), including its prerequisites. The 3.7L and 5.0L heater procedures do not specify starter removal.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the heater
steps.body: Observe how the heater wiring is routed and secured, then disconnect its electrical connector. Remove the block heater using the correct engine procedure. Use the illustration for your selected engine to identify the connector and heater location.

steps.title: Install the heater and restore its wiring
steps.body: Install the heater and tighten it to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm), as specified for each of these engines. Reconnect the electrical connector and secure the wiring away from rotating or hot components. Reinstall the starter on the 2.3L by reversing its removal procedure.

steps.title: Fill and bleed the system
steps.body: Complete the engine-specific filling and bleeding procedure after reassembly. Follow that procedure’s full sequence so the cooling system is restored after heater removal.

watchFor.title: Wiring exposed to heat or movement
watchFor.body: A connected plug is not enough: the heater wiring must also be routed and secured away from hot and rotating parts.

watchFor.title: A different leak source on the 3.7L
watchFor.body: Oil or coolant at the front-left weep hole behind the generator points to the channel cover plate’s sealing system, not automatically to the block heater.

notes: The replacement sequence does not establish an electrical diagnosis; heater performance testing requires the applicable diagnostic information.

diagnostics.finding: Oil or coolant leaks from the 3.7L weep hole behind the generator.
diagnostics.meaning: The cooling-system description identifies a failed channel cover plate gasket and requires replacement of the plate.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable engine repair path for the channel cover plate instead of treating this location as evidence for heater replacement.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical and wiring completion
verification.body: Verify the heater was tightened to specification, its connector is attached and its wiring is secured clear of the stated hazards. Confirm starter reinstallation on the 2.3L.

verification.title: Record coolant-service completion
verification.body: Record the engine variant and completion of its filling and bleeding procedure, keeping that result distinct from any separate heater electrical test.

guides.title: Replace ignition coils on the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Remove and inspect coil-on-plug units, replace damaged assemblies or boots as specified, and restore the correct engine-specific connections and tightening.
guides.introduction: A coil-on-plug unit supplies ignition voltage directly to its spark plug through an insulated boot. This job removes the unit and inspects it for physical damage before refitting or replacement. The engines share that basic arrangement, but their access requirements, replacement instructions and mounting-bolt tightening differ.
guides.why: Cleaning around a seated coil keeps loose material from falling into the opening during removal. A slight twist releases the boot seal without forcing it straight upward. Correct tightening matters because the mounting instructions range from a fixed torque to torque followed by an additional angle.

when.summary: When a coil requires removal or replacement, or inspection reveals cracks, rips or tears.
notes: Select the engine procedure before starting; the 3.7L right-hand coils require upper intake-manifold removal.

prepare.title: Match tools to the engine branch
prepare.detail: Provide compressed air for cleaning, suitable hand tools and a torque wrench. The 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L also require controlled angle tightening. Right-hand access on the 3.7L requires the capability and prerequisites in the upper intake-manifold procedure.

steps.title: Expose the coils on the 2.3L or 3.7L
steps.body: On the [2.3L](#/document/G1673188), disconnect the battery through the linked procedure, then remove the appearance-cover nuts, bolts and cover. On the [3.7L](#/document/G1675558), remove the upper intake manifold for right-hand access. That manifold-removal instruction applies to the right-hand bank.

steps.title: Expose the coils on the V8 engines
steps.body: On the [5.0L](#/document/G1675574), remove the appearance cover, release the positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve coupling and crankcase ventilation tube coupling, and move them aside before removing the coil covers. On the [5.2L](#/document/G1805373), release the PCV hose couplings, position the hoses out of the way and remove the coil covers.

steps.title: Disconnect, clean and lift out the coils
steps.body: Follow the selected procedure's connector and cleaning sequence. On the 2.3L, release the harness retainers and slide back any cover over a connector locking tab before depressing it. Use compressed air around the coils while they are still seated; the 3.7L places this cleaning before connector disconnection. Remove the mounting bolts, then use a slight twisting motion to release each coil's seal and lift it out.

steps.title: Inspect the specified replaceable part
steps.body: For the 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L, inspect the coil-on-plug assembly for cracks, rips or tears and replace damaged assemblies. The 3.7L instruction specifically calls for replacing rubber boots with this damage. Use that distinction when deciding which part needs renewal.

steps.title: Install and tighten for the exact engine
steps.body: Install the coils and mounting bolts. The 2.3L requires 89 lb.in (10 Nm). The 3.7L requires 62 lb.in (7 Nm), then 50°. Both V8 procedures require 62 lb.in (7 Nm), then 45°. Reconnect the electrical connectors; on the 2.3L, secure the locking tabs and harness retainers.

steps.title: Restore the access components
steps.body: Refit the 3.7L upper intake manifold if removed. On the V8s, refit the coil covers and reconnect the ventilation couplings. Before fitting the 5.0L appearance cover, move any grommets retained in the cover back onto the intake manifold. On the 2.3L, refit the appearance cover, tighten its fasteners to 80 lb.in (9 Nm) and reconnect the battery through its procedure.

watchFor.title: Connector locks and seals
watchFor.body: Release the locking tab rather than pulling against it. Use the specified slight twist when lifting a coil whose boot seal remains attached.

notes: Use the procedure and illustration for your selected engine to identify the coils and their access requirements.

diagnostics.finding: Cracks, rips or tears are visible.
diagnostics.meaning: The assembly or rubber boot has physical damage requiring the engine-specific replacement action.
diagnostics.next: Replace the damaged assembly on the 2.3L, 5.0L or 5.2L; renew the damaged rubber boot on the 3.7L.

verification.title: Confirm tightening and restoration
verification.body: Check that the selected engine's torque and angle were completed, connectors are secured, and disturbed retainers, ventilation couplings and covers are restored. Confirm battery reconnection on the 2.3L and manifold installation where required on the 3.7L.

guides.title: Replace the 5.2L 3160 manual-transmission fluid temperature sensor
guides.summary: Raise the vehicle safely, replace the transmission fluid temperature sensor and complete the specified transmission refill.
guides.introduction: The transmission fluid temperature (TFT) sensor measures the temperature of the lubricant inside the 3160 manual transmission. This gearbox transfers engine torque to the driveshaft and includes an oil pump for fluid cooling. Sensor replacement combines an electrical disconnection with work at the transmission housing and the listed drain-and-refill sequence.
guides.why: Safe underbody access is the first requirement. Correct tightening then matters at both the drain plug and sensor, which have different torque specifications. Completing the transmission-specific filling procedure restores the fluid needed by the gearbox; sensor installation alone does not finish the job.

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies a faulty TFT sensor on the 5.2L vehicle with the 3160 manual transmission.
notes: The replacement procedure supplies no electrical fault thresholds; establish the need for replacement through diagnosis.

prepare.title: Arrange safe lifting
prepare.detail: Use a suitable hoist and follow [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Identify the prescribed lifting points by their stamped triangles and check adapter clearance around suspension, exhaust, steering and axle components.

prepare.title: Prepare fluid-service equipment
prepare.detail: Have a drain container, suitable removal tools and torque tools. Obtain the fluid and filling equipment required by [Transmission Draining and Filling](#/document/G1794233) for this 3160 transmission.

steps.title: Position the vehicle on the hoist
steps.body: Place the transmission in NEUTRAL and position the vehicle on the hoist. Check for underbody interference before using a drive-on lift, and position lifting adapters carefully before raising the vehicle.

steps.title: Drain the transmission
steps.body: Follow the listed removal sequence by removing the drain plug and draining the fluid. The procedure also expressly requires drainage when transmission disassembly is needed. The drain plug's installation torque is 21 lb.ft (28 Nm).

steps.title: Remove the sensor
steps.body: Disconnect the TFT sensor electrical connector, then remove the sensor. Follow [the sensor removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1809313) for identification and access.

steps.title: Install and reconnect the sensor
steps.body: Install the TFT sensor and tighten it to 97 lb.in (11 Nm), then connect its electrical connector. Use the sensor specification at this step, keeping it distinct from the drain-plug torque.

steps.title: Complete the transmission refill
steps.body: Ensure the drain plug is installed to its specified torque, then fill the transmission using the linked 3160 draining and filling procedure. Follow that procedure for the correct fluid and filling requirements.

watchFor.title: Unsupported underbody work
watchFor.body: Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. If using a jack, support the vehicle with floor stands. The emergency wheel-change jack is unsuitable for this service.

watchFor.title: Incorrect lifting contact
watchFor.body: Do not lift against either bumper. Incorrect lift points or adapter placement can damage components or allow the vehicle to shift.

notes: The 3160 overview describes its fluid as a service-life fill. Draining and refilling for this repair does not establish a routine change interval.

verification.title: Confirm installation completion
verification.body: Check that the sensor is tightened, its electrical connector is connected and the transmission filling procedure is complete.

verification.title: Record the service result
verification.body: Record the sensor and drain-plug tightening values and completion of the 3160 refill. Keep the original diagnostic finding with the repair record so installation completion remains distinct from confirmation that the original concern is resolved.

guides.title: Replace the evaporative emission canister
guides.summary: Remove and reinstall the underbody vapor canister using the correct engine procedure, including the additional shield and differential-cooler access on the 5.2L.
guides.introduction: The evaporative emission (EVAP) canister stores fuel vapor as part of the system connecting the fuel tank and purge path to the engine intake. It is a separate component from the purge valve. Replacement involves its underbody mountings, electrical connector, vapor couplings and vent hose. The main sequence is similar across engines, but the 5.2L requires additional access work.
guides.why: Fuel vapor can form highly flammable mixtures even though this job does not open a liquid-fuel supply line. Battery isolation and ignition-source control are essential. The canister is lowered before its vapor connections are released, so controlling its movement avoids loading the attached hoses. Correct engine selection also keeps shield and cooler fasteners from being confused with canister mountings.

when.summary: When a repair requires removal or replacement of the EVAP canister.
notes: Use the engine-specific procedure; the 5.2L shield and differential-cooler access steps are additional to the common canister work.

prepare.title: Fuel-vapor precautions
prepare.detail: Exclude smoking, lighted tobacco and open flames. The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.2L procedures also explicitly prohibit carrying personal electronic devices near the work. Follow the referenced fuel-system safety precautions for the 5.0L.

prepare.title: Safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the triangle-marked lifting points. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack, and do not use the emergency tire-changing jack for this job. Check lift clearance and protect suspension, exhaust, steering and axle components when positioning the lift.

prepare.title: Connection and tightening capability
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools and torque equipment, plus the applicable battery and quick-release coupling procedures. Installation torques appear alongside removal steps in each engine's canister procedure.

steps.title: Lift the vehicle and isolate the battery
steps.body: Position the vehicle on a hoist using [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Disconnect the battery ground cable using [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356) before disturbing the canister electrical connection. For the 5.0L, follow the [fuel-system safety precautions](#/document/G1693188) referenced by its procedure.

steps.title: Open the 5.2L shield access
steps.body: For the 5.2L only, follow [its canister procedure](#/document/G1805778): remove the rear underbody shield rear bolts, push-pin retainers, front bolts and rivet-style push-pin retainers in the stated order. These fastener groups have different installation requirements.

steps.title: Position the 5.2L cooler components aside
steps.body: On the 5.2L, remove the retainers and position the rear differential fluid cooler aside. Then remove the retainer and position its pump bracket aside. Keep the attached assemblies controlled while gaining access to the canister.

steps.title: Remove the electrical connection and bracket
steps.body: For every engine, disconnect the canister electrical connector. Remove the bracket bolts, pin-type retainers and bracket, following the selected engine procedure so each attachment can be restored correctly.

steps.title: Lower the canister
steps.body: Remove the remaining mounting bolts, then remove the nuts and lower the canister. Support its movement because the vapor couplings and vent hose are still connected at this stage.

steps.title: Release the vapor connections
steps.body: Disconnect the quick-connect couplings using the engine-specific coupling procedure. The 5.2L canister instructions explicitly refer to the 5.0L coupling procedure. Disconnect the vent hose and remove the canister.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Reconnect the vent hose and vapor couplings, raise and secure the canister, and restore its bracket and electrical connection. Use the torque for each fastener group in the selected engine procedure. On the 5.2L, restore the cooler, pump bracket and shield through the reverse access sequence. Complete battery reconnection using its referenced procedure.

watchFor.title: Hoses carrying the canister's weight
watchFor.body: Lower the canister under control until its connections can be released.

watchFor.title: Mixed installation settings
watchFor.body: The bracket, canister mountings and 5.2L access hardware do not all share one tightening value.

notes: Follow the procedure for your selected engine to identify the canister connections and complete its access sequence.

verification.title: Check restored connections
verification.body: Confirm the quick-connect couplings, vent hose and electrical connector are restored and the canister and bracket are secured.

verification.title: Check variant-specific completion
verification.body: On the 5.2L, confirm the differential cooler, pump bracket and underbody shield are reinstalled. Confirm battery reconnection is complete for every variant.

verification.title: Record tightening completion
verification.body: Record the engine procedure used and completion of its installation torque requirements, including the separate 5.2L access hardware where applicable.

guides.title: Replace the air distribution door actuator
guides.summary: Remove and refit the electric actuator that positions the climate system’s air distribution door.
guides.introduction: The air distribution door directs conditioned air toward the selected outlets, and its electric actuator moves that door. This is a different function from changing blower speed or outlet temperature. Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) responds to the control-panel selections, while Dual Automatic Temperature Control (DATC) maintains a selected cabin temperature and allows driver overrides. This job replaces the distribution actuator without dismantling the climate-control unit.
guides.why: The retainers hold the actuator in its operating position, while the electrical connector allows it to receive electrical commands. Both attachments must be released during removal and restored during installation. Supporting the actuator while disconnecting it keeps its weight from hanging on the wiring.
searchTerms: airflow does not follow outlet selection
climate control air coming from wrong outlets

when.summary: When diagnosis has identified the air distribution door actuator as needing removal or replacement.
notes: An outlet-selection complaint warrants investigation; it does not establish by itself that the actuator has failed.

prepare.title: Identify the actuator and its attachments
prepare.detail: Use the illustration to distinguish the actuator housing, its two retainers and its electrical connector from the surrounding ductwork.

prepare.title: Arrange controlled access
prepare.detail: Have hand tools suited to the illustrated retainers and enough access to support the housing during removal.

steps.title: Match the component to the illustration
steps.body: Follow the [actuator removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1676754). Locate both retainers and the connector before beginning so that each attachment can be released deliberately.

steps.title: Remove the retainers
steps.body: Support the actuator and remove its retainers. These secure the housing; removing them frees the actuator for the next operation but leaves its electrical connection attached.

steps.title: Remove and disconnect the actuator
steps.body: Move the actuator out of its installed position and disconnect its electrical connector. Keep the housing supported until the connector is free rather than pulling it away by the harness.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Reconnect the electrical connector, return the actuator to its installed position and reinstall the retainers. Complete both the electrical connection and the mechanical attachment before finishing.

watchFor.title: Confusing distribution with other climate functions
watchFor.body: Blower speed and temperature selection are separate controls. A complaint about either function does not identify this actuator as the cause.

watchFor.title: An unfinished attachment
watchFor.body: A connected plug does not secure the housing, and installed retainers do not establish that the connector has been restored.

notes: This is an actuator removal and installation procedure; it does not provide an electrical fault-isolation test or an initialization sequence.

verification.title: Check the completed installation
verification.body: Confirm that the actuator is back in its installed position, both retainers are restored and the electrical connector is connected.

procedures.purpose: Complete removal and reverse-order installation of the air distribution door actuator.

guides.title: Rebuild the output-shaft subassembly in the 3160 six-speed manual transmission
guides.summary: Strip and rebuild the output-shaft gears, bearings and synchronizers with controlled pressing, heating and component alignment.
guides.introduction: The 3160 transmission’s output shaft transfers drive toward the rear differential. Its gears remain meshed with their partners, while synchronizer sleeves lock the selected gear to the shaft. The first–second sleeve selects those two ratios; the fifth–sixth sleeve also provides the direct connection between input and output shafts in fifth gear. This job covers the output-shaft bench subassembly after it has been removed from the gearbox.
guides.why: The gears, roller bearings, synchronizer assemblies and detents form an ordered stack. Incorrect sleeve alignment can disrupt the relationship between the sleeve and its detents. The specified heating temporarily expands tightly fitted bearing components for assembly, but excessive temperature or heating time can damage them. This requires gearbox rebuilding experience rather than ordinary external transmission service skills.

when.summary: During a gearbox repair that requires output-shaft gear, bearing or synchronizer disassembly.
notes: The bench procedure begins with the shaft accessible; transmission removal and case disassembly are separate work.

prepare.title: Provide the pressing equipment
prepare.detail: A hydraulic press and bearing separator are required for the specified disassembly operations. The operator must be able to support the assembly appropriately while separating fitted components.

prepare.title: Control heat and component order
prepare.detail: Provide a controlled means of heating and monitoring temperature and time. Arrange the removed components in their working order, keeping synchronizer assemblies and detents identifiable.

steps.title: Remove the sixth-gear end components
steps.body: Remove the snap ring, then the fifth–sixth synchronizer hub, sleeve and detents. Lift off the sixth-gear three-piece synchronizer assembly, sixth gear and its roller bearing in that order.

steps.title: Press off the first-gear group
steps.body: Use the hydraulic press and bearing separator to remove the roller bearing and first gear. Then remove the first-gear roller bearing and its three-piece synchronizer assembly, retaining their order for rebuilding.

steps.title: Separate the second-gear group
steps.body: With the press and bearing separator, remove second gear, the first–second synchronizer hub and sleeve, and the first-gear roller-bearing inner race. Remove the second-gear roller bearing to finish the specified strip.

steps.title: Rebuild second gear and its synchronizer
steps.body: Install the second-gear roller bearing, second gear and its three-piece synchronizer assembly. Install the first–second hub, sleeve and three detents. Align the sleeve’s indented internal splines with the hub’s detent slots.

steps.title: Fit the first-gear bearing race
steps.body: Heat the first-gear bearing race to 260°F and install it on the output shaft. Do not exceed that temperature or heat the component for longer than 15 minutes.

steps.title: Rebuild first gear
steps.body: Install the first-gear three-piece synchronizer assembly, followed by the roller bearing and first gear. Align the synchronizer with the slot in the gear so the mating features occupy their intended positions.

steps.title: Fit the rear bearing and sixth gear
steps.body: Heat the rear bearing to 260°F and install it, observing the same 15-minute maximum heating time. Install the sixth-gear roller bearing, sixth gear and its three-piece synchronizer assembly.

steps.title: Complete the fifth–sixth synchronizer
steps.body: Install the hub, sleeve and detents, then install the snap ring. Again, align the sleeve’s indented internal splines with the hub’s detent slots. Use the complete output-shaft procedure to check the final component sequence.

watchFor.title: Misaligned sleeve features
watchFor.body: Check the indented splines against the detent slots on both synchronizer hubs before completing assembly.

watchFor.title: Uncontrolled heating
watchFor.body: Both heated components have an explicit temperature and time limit; prolonged heating is not an acceptable way to resolve a fitting problem.

notes: Identify the cause of a gear-selection complaint before committing to an output-shaft rebuild.

verification.title: Check the specified assembly relationships
verification.body: Confirm both sleeve-to-detent alignments, the first-gear synchronizer-to-slot alignment and installation of the final snap ring.

verification.title: Record the controlled assembly
verification.body: Record the bearing-race and rear-bearing heating temperatures and durations before handing the shaft back to the gearbox assembly operation.

Explain gear powerflow and identify output-shaft gears, bearings, hubs, sleeves and detents.

guides.title: Replace the dashboard sunload sensor
guides.summary: Release the sunload sensor with an interior trim remover, disconnect its electrical connector and install the replacement in reverse order.
guides.introduction: The sunload sensor detects sunlight, providing an indication of the solar heat reaching the vehicle. It sits on the upper instrument panel near the windshield, as shown in the illustration. Replacement involves a small clipped sensor and its electrical connector. The work is compact, but controlled trim handling matters because the sensor must be released before its wiring can be disconnected.
guides.why: The sensor housing has retaining features on its sides. Releasing those features with the specified interior trim remover avoids treating the surrounding dashboard as a part that must be dismantled. Separating the electrical connector after lifting the sensor also keeps the wire from becoming the means of pulling the assembly out.

when.summary: When the sunload sensor has been identified for replacement.
notes: This replacement sequence does not establish whether a climate-control complaint is caused by the sensor.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified trim tool
prepare.detail: Use an interior trim remover. Allow clear access to the sensor on top of the instrument panel and enough room to handle its connector once the housing is released.

prepare.title: Identify the retained housing
prepare.detail: Use the [sunload sensor illustration](#/document/G1676821) to locate the sensor and recognize its side retaining features before applying the tool.

steps.title: Position the trim remover
steps.body: Work at the sensor's edge with the interior trim remover. Keep the action focused on releasing the clipped housing from the instrument panel.

steps.title: Release and lift the sensor
steps.body: Free the sensor from its retaining features and lift it far enough to reach the electrical connector. Keep the connected wiring from carrying the removal force.

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical connector
steps.body: Support the released sensor while disconnecting its plug. The housing can then be removed completely without pulling on the wiring.

steps.title: Connect and seat the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: reconnect the electrical connector, position the sensor in its opening and engage its retaining features.

watchFor.title: Housing still retained
watchFor.body: If the sensor resists lifting, check whether its retaining features have released before increasing force.

watchFor.title: Connector overlooked during installation
watchFor.body: Reconnect the plug before seating the sensor; the mechanical installation alone does not restore its electrical connection.

notes: Climate-control systems use different operating strategies: manual control follows panel selections, while dual automatic control maintains selected cabin temperatures. Use the fitted climate-control system’s operating mode when checking its response after the sensor is replaced.

verification.title: Confirm installation
verification.body: Check that the electrical connector is connected and the sensor's retaining features hold it in its installed position.

procedures.purpose: Sunload sensor removal and installation using an interior trim remover.

guides.title: Rebuild the 5.2L 3160 manual transmission extension housing
guides.summary: Strip the extension-housing subassembly, inspect its shift-shaft bearings and rebuild the specified bearing, reverse-gear and sensor components.
guides.introduction: The aluminum extension housing forms the rear section of the 3160 six-speed manual transmission. It carries shaft-support bearings, shift-shaft bearings, seals and sensor components, along with the reverse idler gear and its pin. The idler participates in reversing output-shaft rotation. This is specialist bench work on an already accessible subassembly, rather than a complete transmission removal and installation job.
guides.why: The inspection distinguishes the shift-shaft bearings from the separately removed output-shaft and countershaft bearings. Damage to a shift-shaft bearing requires a new extension housing. Keeping those parts distinct prevents a rebuild from retaining a housing that the inspection has already ruled out.

when.summary: When transmission repair requires extension-housing disassembly or its shift-shaft bearings need inspection.
notes: This procedure begins at the subassembly stage; transmission removal and housing separation require their own procedures.
The transmission fluid temperature sensor is handled only if fitted.

prepare.title: Provide transmission bench-work capability
prepare.detail: Arrange a clean work area and the capability to handle seals, bearings and retaining rings without damaging the housing. Use the [extension-housing procedure](#/document/G1849275) for the illustrated component locations.

prepare.title: Keep components identifiable
prepare.detail: Distinguish the output-shaft bearing and ring from the countershaft bearing and ring. Have suitable torque equipment for the reverse gear pin bolt and sensor fasteners.

steps.title: Remove the fitted sensors
steps.body: If equipped, remove the transmission fluid temperature (TFT) sensor. Then remove the speed-sensor bolt and speed sensor. The temperature-sensor branch is conditional; the speed sensor is part of the main sequence.

steps.title: Remove the seals and tone wheel
steps.body: Remove the output shaft seal, then the tone wheel, followed by the manual shaft seal. Discard the removed output seal. Inspect the tone wheel and replace it if damaged, following the [matching output-seal procedure](#/document/G1794237). The tone wheel belongs to the speed-sensing arrangement; keep it identifiable for the later transmission assembly stage.

steps.title: Remove the reverse idler components
steps.body: Remove the bolt, reverse gear pin and reverse idler gear. Keep these components together so the pin and its fastening can be identified during assembly.

steps.title: Remove the shaft-support bearings
steps.body: Remove the retaining ring and output-shaft bearing first. Then remove the retaining ring and countershaft bearing. These are separate from the shift-shaft bearings inspected inside the housing.

steps.title: Clean and inspect the shift-shaft bearings
steps.body: Clean the shift-shaft bearings and inspect them for damage, using the highlighted locations in the illustration. If damage is found, install a new extension housing; the specified repair decision is housing replacement.

steps.title: Install the bearings and reverse gear
steps.body: Install the countershaft bearing and retaining ring, followed by the output-shaft bearing and retaining ring. Install the reverse idler gear, reverse gear pin and bolt. Tighten that bolt to 106 lb.in (12 Nm).

steps.title: Fit the manual shaft seal and sensors
steps.body: Install the manual shaft seal. Install the speed sensor and tighten its bolt to 71 lb.in (8 Nm). If fitted, install the TFT sensor and tighten it to 97 lb.in (11 Nm).

steps.title: Continue through the complete transmission assembly sequence
steps.body: The completed housing is a subassembly. Follow [3160 transmission assembly](#/document/G1849280) to install the housing and its remaining transmission components in order. That sequence fits the tone wheel after the housing is installed, then installs a new output seal with tools 205-199 and 308-959, followed by the output flange, washer and new nut. Keep those later operations in that sequence rather than fitting the seal prematurely on the loose housing.

watchFor.title: Shift-shaft bearing damage
watchFor.body: Do not confuse this finding with damage limited to a removable shaft-support bearing. The specified response to damaged shift-shaft bearings is a new housing.

watchFor.title: Different fastener torques
watchFor.body: The reverse gear pin bolt, speed-sensor bolt and optional TFT sensor have different tightening values.

notes: The output seal and tone wheel are fitted during the later transmission assembly stage. Completing the housing’s bench work is the handoff to that sequence.

diagnostics.finding: Damage found while cleaning and inspecting a shift-shaft bearing.
diagnostics.meaning: The extension housing requires replacement under this procedure.
diagnostics.next: Install a new extension housing before continuing the subassembly build.

verification.title: Check the specified assembly work
verification.body: Confirm that both shaft-support bearings and retaining rings, the reverse idler components, manual shaft seal and applicable sensors have been installed.

verification.title: Record the housing decision
verification.body: Record the shift-shaft bearing inspection result and whether the housing was retained or replaced. Before the complete transmission is finished, confirm that the later assembly sequence has restored the tone wheel, new output seal and output flange.

Complete 3160 transmission assembly, including housing installation followed by tone wheel, new output seal and flange restoration.
Matching output-seal renewal requirement, tone-wheel inspection and the dedicated seal-installer arrangement.

guides.title: Adjust the parking brake cable
guides.summary: Set parking brake cable tension by measuring rear caliper lever clearance, cycling the mechanism and making the final adjustment.
guides.introduction: The parking brake cable transfers movement from the parking brake control to mechanical levers on the rear calipers. The adjustment nut changes cable tension, which changes where those levers sit relative to their stops. This job establishes that setting through measured clearances; it does not, by itself, diagnose the cause of poor parking brake operation.
guides.why: The procedure uses an initial setting followed by repeated application and release before the final adjustment. Moving the mechanism through its working travel makes that sequence important. Lever clearance is the adjustment reference, so tightening the nut by feel cannot establish the specified result.

when.summary: When the parking brake cable setting requires adjustment.
notes: Use the measured lever clearances to establish the setting rather than judging cable tension alone.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underside access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points, identified by stamped triangles. Position adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering components. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare to measure the levers
prepare.detail: Have a feeler gauge and suitable access to the adjustment nut and both caliper lever stops. The illustrated adjustment nut and lever gap identify the two places involved in the setting.

steps.title: Position the vehicle
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist using the linked lifting procedure. Establish secure access before working at the cable adjustment mechanism.

steps.title: Establish the initial clearance
steps.body: Tighten the parking brake cable adjustment nut until one or both caliper levers are 2.0 mm away from their stops. Use the feeler gauge to measure the gap.

steps.title: Cycle the parking brake
steps.body: Fully apply and release the parking brake 5 times. Complete each application and release before beginning the next, retaining this stage between the initial and final settings.

steps.title: Make the final adjustment
steps.body: After the cycling stage, tighten the adjustment nut until one or both caliper levers are 1.0 mm away from their stops. Measure again with the feeler gauge; the initial clearance is not the finished setting.

watchFor.title: Unnecessary tightening to match both sides
watchFor.body: The specified condition is one or both levers at the stated clearance. Do not continue tightening solely to make the opposite lever match.

notes: The vehicle's emergency jack is intended for changing a deflated tire, not for providing access for this adjustment.

verification.title: Confirm and record the final setting
verification.body: Confirm that one or both lever gaps measure 1.0 mm after the prescribed cycling and adjustment sequence. Record the measured result and completion of the 5 full applications and releases.

procedures.purpose: Complete parking brake cable adjustment sequence, including initial clearance, cycling and final clearance.
Correct lifting points, hoist positioning and vehicle-support precautions.

applicability.equipment: Rear calipers with parking-brake operating levers; excludes the separate SVT parking-brake shoe arrangement

guides.title: Replace a B-pillar side impact sensor
guides.summary: Depower the restraint system, access and replace the side impact sensor with flush mounting surfaces, then restore and repower the system.
guides.introduction: The B-pillar side impact sensor contributes information used by the restraints control module to assess a side impact. The module considers sensor inputs before deciding whether restraint deployment is necessary. Replacing this sensor involves more than exchanging an electrical part: its mounting, connection and the prescribed supplemental restraint system (SRS) power procedures are essential parts of the repair.
guides.why: These are critical repair steps for correct restraint operation during a crash. The sensor must attach flush against smooth mating surfaces, and its mounting bolt must be tightened correctly. Depowering before disconnection and repowering after reassembly are separate required procedures; an improvised power-disconnection step is not a substitute for following them.

when.summary: When diagnosis or an applicable restraint repair calls for replacement of a B-pillar side impact sensor.
notes: An airbag warning indicator alone does not establish that this sensor is defective.

prepare.title: Provide restraint-system service capability
prepare.detail: Use a technician equipped to follow the complete SRS depowering and repowering procedures. Have both procedures available before disturbing the sensor connection.

prepare.title: Confirm the sensor and coupe access
prepare.detail: Identify the fitted second-row side impact sensor and use the coupe loadspace-trim access procedure. Body style and component identification must agree before restraint work begins.

prepare.title: Prepare for the mounting requirement
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools and a torque wrench capable of 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm). Allow access to inspect both sensor mating surfaces before installation.

steps.title: Depower the SRS
steps.body: Complete the linked SRS Depowering procedure before working on the sensor. Follow its full sequence and prerequisites rather than treating ignition-off as the completed preparation.

steps.title: Remove the loadspace trim
steps.body: Use the coupe loadspace trim procedure to expose the identified sensor. Follow the specified trim-removal path to gain access without guessing at concealed attachments.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the sensor
steps.body: Use the illustration to identify the electrical connector, mounting bolt and sensor. Disconnect the connector, remove the bolt and then remove the side impact sensor, preserving that order.

steps.title: Establish a flush mounting
steps.body: Check that the impact sensor mating surfaces are smooth and allow flush attachment. Resolve anything preventing that contact before fitting the sensor, then install the mounting bolt and tighten it to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the connection and trim
steps.body: Complete the remaining installation by reversing removal. Reconnect the sensor electrical connector and restore the coupe loadspace trim.

steps.title: Repower the restraint system
steps.body: Carry out the linked SRS Repowering procedure after installation. Follow its complete sequence to finish restoring the system; sensor installation alone does not complete this job.

watchFor.title: A sensor that does not sit flush
watchFor.body: Do not use bolt tightening to compensate for mating surfaces that prevent flush attachment. Smooth, flush contact is an explicit installation requirement.

watchFor.title: Incomplete restraint-system procedures
watchFor.body: Skipping a prescribed step can affect restraint operation during a crash even when the sensor appears physically secure.

notes: The second-row side impact sensor application described here is for the coupe. A convertible trim-access reference does not establish that the convertible uses this sensor.

diagnostics.finding: An airbag warning indicator remains illuminated.
diagnostics.meaning: The restraint controller monitors multiple inputs and connections, so a warning does not identify this sensor as the cause.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable restraint-system diagnosis rather than assuming another sensor replacement is required.

verification.title: Confirm the installed condition
verification.body: Confirm flush sensor mounting, the specified bolt tightening, the restored electrical connection and completed trim installation.

verification.title: Record system restoration
verification.body: Record the side serviced and the outcome of the prescribed repowering procedure. Document any remaining restraint warning for diagnosis before considering the repair complete.

guides.title: Remove and install the side curtain airbag
guides.summary: Depower the restraint system, remove the roof-mounted curtain assembly and reinstall it with correct attachment, connector locking and repowering.
guides.introduction: The side curtain airbag is a roof-mounted part of the supplemental restraint system (SRS). The restraints control module (RCM) monitors sensor inputs and commands the appropriate restraint components when it determines that deployment is needed. This repair removes the curtain assembly from behind the headliner, then restores its mounting and electrical connection. Its installed position matters because the curtain must deploy correctly along the roofline.
guides.why: This work controls two serious risks: accidental deployment during repair and incorrect deployment during a crash. Depowering protects the repair operation, while sound roof structure, correct curtain orientation and the specified fastening sequence protect its installed function. Connector locking also matters electrically; a connector can make contact while its assurance tab remains incompletely seated.

when.summary: When side curtain airbag removal or replacement is required and SRS service capability is available.
notes: An illuminated airbag warning indicator alone does not establish that the curtain assembly needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: The person doing the work must be able to follow the complete SRS depowering and repowering procedures and handle deployable-component connectors correctly.

prepare.title: Prepare access and fastening information
prepare.detail: Have the headliner procedure, suitable screw and retainer tools, and torque equipment. Use the numbered installation diagram to identify the screw positions and tightening sequence.

prepare.title: Allow for mounting repairs
prepare.detail: Installation requires inspection of the roofline. Damaged sheet metal must be restored to its original condition and structural integrity, damaged fasteners renewed and foreign material removed.

steps.title: Depower the SRS
steps.body: Complete [SRS Depowering](#/document/G1696297) before disturbing the curtain connection. Follow the full procedure precisely; its requirements govern safe disconnection and later reconnection.

steps.title: Remove the headliner
steps.body: Follow [Headliner](#/document/G1692615) to expose the curtain and its attachments. This provides access to the connector, screw groups and retainers without pulling against concealed fixings.

steps.title: Disconnect and release the screw groups
steps.body: In the order shown in [Side Curtain Airbag](#/document/G1696310), disconnect the electrical connector and remove the screws, then remove the next screw group. Note the unique installation instructions for these locations before proceeding.

steps.title: Release the retainers and T-tab
steps.body: Remove the A-pillar pin-type retainers, disengage the retainer and move the curtain away from the A-pillar. Disengage the remaining pin-type retainers, remove the final pin-type retainer, then slide the assembly forward and out to disengage its T-tab from the sheet metal.

steps.title: Prepare the roofline for installation
steps.body: Inspect the mounting area and resolve roofline damage before fitting the curtain. Remove foreign material and replace damaged fasteners. Check the curtain orientation so it is not twisted 360° between attachment points.

steps.title: Refit and tighten in sequence
steps.body: Reverse removal, following the installation diagram for attachment and screw positions. Keep the SRS depowered before reconnecting the component. Tighten screws 1 and 2 to 106 lb.in (12 Nm), then screws 3 through 7 to 80 lb.in (9 Nm), in the illustrated sequence.

steps.title: Restore trim and repower
steps.body: Complete headliner reinstallation and then follow [SRS Repowering](#/document/G1696298). Repowering is the final required phase of the curtain installation.

watchFor.title: Roofline damage or a twisted curtain
watchFor.body: Either can interfere with correct deployment. Resolve structural damage and curtain orientation before closing the headliner.

watchFor.title: Reconnection while powered
watchFor.body: The restraint system must be depowered before the component is reconnected; incorrect handling can cause accidental deployment.

notes: The numbered installation diagram is essential for identifying the two screw groups; do not infer their positions from the removal view.

diagnostics.finding: The deployable-component connector is attached, but its Connector Position Assurance (CPA) tab is not fully seated.
diagnostics.meaning: The connector pins can make contact while the component's shorting bars remain applied. The RCM can detect resistance below threshold and illuminate the airbag warning indicator.
diagnostics.next: Treat connector seating as a diagnostic consideration rather than proof of a failed curtain. Follow SRS depowering before correcting the connection, then complete the prescribed repowering process.

verification.title: Check installation before covering it
verification.body: Confirm roofline condition, curtain orientation, retainer and T-tab engagement, connector locking and completion of the numbered screw-tightening sequence.

verification.title: Record the repowering result
verification.body: Record completion of the repowering procedure and whether the airbag warning indicator reports a fault afterward. A remaining warning requires diagnosis rather than assuming the replacement curtain is defective.

guides.title: Replace the in-tank fuel pump and sender unit
guides.summary: Release fuel pressure, lower the tank level and replace the pump-and-sender assembly through the rear-seat access opening with a new seal.
guides.introduction: The tank-mounted assembly supplies pressurized fuel and carries the sender that reports fuel level. Replacement involves connections both above the tank and inside it. Access is through an opening beneath the rear seat cushion, but the tank must first be prepared so fuel sits below the unit's mounting flange. The four engine procedures share this access sequence while retaining engine-specific pressure-release and coupling instructions.
guides.why: Fuel pressure can remain after pump operation stops, so pressure release must precede disconnection. Lowering the fuel level addresses a separate problem: fuel reaching the open mounting flange. During installation, a new O-ring and correctly engaged alignment tabs establish the prescribed seal and unit position before the lock ring is tightened.

when.summary: When diagnosis calls for replacement of the tank-mounted fuel pump and sender assembly.
notes: The removal sequence does not diagnose a fuel-pressure or gauge complaint.
Use the matching 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L procedure and replacement assembly.

prepare.title: Arrange controlled fuel recovery
prepare.detail: Provide fuel tanker 292-00004, the supplemental refueling adapter from the luggage compartment, and a 6 ft. length of 5/8 in. semi-rigid fuel drain tube.

prepare.title: Prepare access and sealing parts
prepare.detail: Have lock-ring tool 310-123 and a new pump-and-sender O-ring seal. Provide access to the rear seat cushion and the engine-matched pressure-release and quick-coupling procedures.

prepare.title: Respect the capless filler
prepare.detail: Use the supplemental adapter for drain-tube entry. The Easy Fuel capless filler assembly must not be modified.

steps.title: Release pressure, then disconnect the battery
steps.body: Complete the fuel-pressure release procedure for the fitted engine. Next, disconnect the battery ground cable using [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356). Do not substitute battery disconnection for pressure release.

steps.title: Drain below the mounting flange
steps.body: Insert the supplemental adapter and specified drain tube through the capless filler until the tube enters the tank. Connect the fuel tanker and remove as much fuel as possible. This removes fuel from the filler pipe and lowers the tank level below the pump mounting flange.

steps.title: Open the rear-seat access
steps.body: Remove the [rear seat cushion](#/document/G1692168), then remove and position aside the pump-and-sender access cover. This exposes the external electrical and fuel connections.

steps.title: Disconnect the external connections
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector and external fuel-tube quick-release coupling. Use the coupling procedure for the fitted engine so the connector is released by its intended mechanism.

steps.title: Unlock and disconnect the assembly
steps.body: Remove the lock ring with tool 310-123. Following the engine-specific removal procedure, disconnect the internal fuel-tube quick coupling and remove the pump-and-sender unit. The internal connection must be released before the assembly is fully removed.

steps.title: Refit with a new seal and correct alignment
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the internal connection and installing a new O-ring seal. Ensure the alignment tabs on the unit and fuel tank meet before tightening the lock ring.

steps.title: Restore the external connections and access
steps.body: Reconnect the external fuel coupling and electrical connector, restore the access cover and rear seat cushion, and complete battery reconnection through its procedure. Follow the applicable coupling instructions during reconnection as well as removal.

steps.title: Prime the fuel system and check for leaks
steps.body: Finish the engine-specific fuel-pressure-release procedure’s restoration sequence. Reconnect the fuel-pump control-module connector used for pressure release; the 5.2L uses two connectors. Restore the rear seat cushion, cycle the ignition key and wait 3 seconds to pressurize the system. Check for leaks before starting the engine, then start it and check for leaks again. Keep this return-to-service check separate from confirming that the mechanical connections are latched.

watchFor.title: Fuel still at the flange
watchFor.body: For a completely full tank, the procedure describes removing approximately 3 gallons to lower the level. The operative requirement is fuel below the mounting flange.

watchFor.title: Tabs not aligned
watchFor.body: Establish the specified alignment before tightening the lock ring; tightening is not a substitute for positioning the assembly.

notes: The 5.2L assembly contains two electric pumps. Its internal equipment should not be inferred from the other engine variants.
The 5.0L and 5.2L descriptions identify a separately serviceable level sender, so a fuel-level complaint alone does not justify complete assembly replacement.

diagnostics.finding: A 5.0L or 5.2L vehicle stopped after a collision.
diagnostics.meaning: Its collision-triggered pump shut-off feature may explain pump inactivity.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable shut-off and diagnostic guidance before treating inactivity as proof of pump failure.

verification.title: Confirm sealing before closing access
verification.body: Confirm a new O-ring was installed and the tank and unit alignment tabs met before lock-ring tightening.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Confirm both internal and external fuel couplings, the electrical connection, access cover, rear seat cushion and battery reconnection are complete.

verification.title: Record both fuel-leak checks
verification.body: Confirm that the fuel-pump control-module connection or connections have been restored and that both the pre-start and running leak checks are complete.

guides.title: Disconnect and reconnect fuel-system spring lock couplings
guides.summary: Separate and reconnect spring lock fuel or vapor tubes using the correct release tool and the pressure-release procedure for your engine.
guides.introduction: A spring lock coupling joins a tube to another fuel-system component using an internal spring retainer. The joint must be deliberately released before the parts can separate. This job covers disconnection and reconnection on the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines, including the external safety clip where fitted. It is normally part of another repair that requires opening a fuel or vapor tube.
guides.why: Pulling against an engaged retainer can damage the connection. Dirt around the retaining clip can also cause damage during separation, while contamination entering an open tube threatens the fine clearances in fuel-injection equipment. Liquid-fuel connections require pressure release before opening; cleanliness remains essential for both liquid and vapor connections.

when.summary: When a spring lock liquid-fuel or vapor tube must be separated for an associated repair.
notes: Identify the engine and whether the connection carries liquid fuel before choosing the prerequisite procedure.

prepare.title: Have the release and cleaning equipment ready
prepare.detail: Use spring lock coupling disconnect tool 310-S039 (T90T-9550-S). Have compressed air, clean engine oil and suitable plugs for all opened tubes and orifices.

prepare.title: Arrange the prerequisite work
prepare.detail: You must be able to complete the engine-specific fuel-pressure release where required and the Battery Disconnect and Connect procedure before separating the joint.

steps.title: Release liquid-fuel pressure
steps.body: For a liquid-fuel tube, complete the pressure-release procedure matching the engine: 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L. This conditional step precedes opening the coupling. The coupling procedure does not call for fuel-pressure release when servicing a vapor-tube connection.

steps.title: Isolate power and clean the coupling
steps.body: Disconnect the battery ground cable using the linked battery procedure. Before separating a connector that will be reused, use compressed air to remove foreign material from its retaining-clip area. Remove the external fuel-tube safety clip if fitted.

steps.title: Release the internal spring and separate the tube
steps.body: Fit the disconnect tool around the tube and push it into the spring lock coupling to release the retainer. Separate the coupling from the tube, then plug every open tube and orifice to prevent contamination during the associated repair.

steps.title: Lubricate and reconnect
steps.body: When ready to close the connection, apply clean engine oil to the tube end. Align the coupling with the tube and push it on until fully seated. Correct alignment allows the tube to enter the connector without forcing the joint sideways.

steps.title: Secure the joint and restore power
steps.body: Refit the safety clip where equipped. Pull on the coupling to confirm engagement, then reconnect the battery ground cable according to the battery procedure.

steps.title: Complete the liquid-fuel service leak checks
steps.body: When a liquid-fuel repair is complete, finish the engine-specific fuel-pressure-release procedure’s restoration sequence. Reconnect the fuel-pump control-module connector used for pressure release; the 5.2L uses two connectors. Restore the rear seat cushion, cycle the ignition key and wait 3 seconds to pressurize the system. Check for leaks before starting the engine, then start it and check for leaks again. Keep this return-to-service check separate from confirming that the mechanical connections are latched.

watchFor.title: Contamination at the retainer
watchFor.body: Clean the clip area before separation and keep opened passages plugged throughout the work.

watchFor.title: A coupling that looks seated but releases
watchFor.body: Appearance alone does not establish retention. Complete the specified pull check before restoring power.

notes: The coupling operation is shared across these engines, but each liquid-fuel pressure-release reference remains engine-specific.

diagnostics.finding: The coupling separates during the pull check.
diagnostics.meaning: Full engagement has not been established.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the seating and retention check before completing the connection.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical retention
verification.body: The coupling must remain engaged when pulled, with its safety clip installed if fitted.

verification.title: Confirm electrical restoration
verification.body: Complete battery ground-cable reconnection through the linked battery procedure.

verification.title: Verify completed liquid-fuel work
verification.body: For a completed liquid-fuel repair, confirm that the fuel-pump control-module connection or connections have been restored and that both the pre-start and running leak checks are complete.

guides.title: Set the correct torque when using an adapter
guides.summary: Match the tool arrangement, measure the right lengths and use the appropriate calculator before tightening a fastener with an offset adapter.
guides.introduction: A torque wrench measures the turning effort applied through its drive. An adapter can move the fastener away from that drive, changing the leverage between your hand and the bolt or nut. That means the number you set on the wrench can differ from the torque the fastener needs. A socket extension and an in-line crowfoot may both help you reach a cramped spot, but their geometry is different.
guides.why: Getting this setup right preserves the intended tightening load while allowing access around nearby parts. The useful question is where the adapter puts the fastener relative to the wrench handle. An adapter extending that reach calls for a different calculation from one pointing back toward the handle; certain right-angle arrangements use the original fastener specification within their stated limits.

when.summary: Before tightening a specified fastener with one of the illustrated adapter or extension arrangements.
notes: This is a tool-setup guide. Take the actual fastener torque, tightening sequence, replacement-fastener requirements and any additional angle stages from the exact repair article.

prepare.title: The fastener specification
prepare.detail: Open the repair article for the component and vehicle configuration you are working on. Keep its torque unit visible; lb-ft, lb-in and Nm are different scales.

prepare.title: A matching tool arrangement
prepare.detail: Compare the direction of the adapter and the position of the socket extension with the linked illustration. Left- and right-hand half-moon setups have separate calculators.

prepare.title: Actual tool dimensions
prepare.detail: Measure wrench length A from the center of the handle to the center of its drive. Measure adapter length B between its drive and fastener centers. Enter the correct length units in the calculator rather than using the tool’s overall end-to-end length.

steps.title: Choose the calculator that matches the geometry
steps.body: For an adapter pointing away from the handle, choose the [straight adapter](#/document/reference-6534a6eae93c), [straight adapter with extension](#/document/reference-72305394e0aa) or [in-line crowfoot](#/document/reference-d7780e6a592b) calculator as appropriate. If the adapter points back toward the handle, use the [reversed adapter with extension](#/document/reference-6943fbf4e2a0) calculator. Similar-looking tools do not guarantee the same leverage.

steps.title: Enter the fastener torque and measured lengths
steps.body: For the straight and crowfoot calculators, enter the specified fastener torque with its unit, then A and B with their length units. Read A from the handle center to the drive center; do not include B in A. The reversed arrangement requires the adapter to be shorter than the wrench because it subtracts from the effective reach.

steps.title: Use the limited half-moon selections when applicable
steps.body: Choose the [left half-moon](#/document/reference-bc8de71f1828) or [right half-moon](#/document/reference-a6c44300b9d8) setup. These calculators cover the listed torque specifications, wrench lengths and adapter combinations. Match the actual tool to those selections and the displayed adapter dimensions. If your combination is absent, choosing the nearest option does not establish a valid setting.

steps.title: Check whether your arrangement needs no correction
steps.body: The illustrated [crowfoot at 90 degrees](#/document/reference-b9ec8cea2317) and [socket extension](#/document/reference-c5d168787f95) arrangements use the original fastener torque. The [straight adapter at 90 degrees](#/document/reference-62fe207918f9) also uses that torque, provided the adapter is no longer than 50.8 mm (2.0 inches). For the [wobble extension](#/document/reference-d7d152a19bd1), keep the angle at or below 15 degrees. Do not extend those allowances to another geometry.

steps.title: Set the wrench using the matching result unit
steps.body: Calculate the required setting where a correction applies. Select the result in the unit marked on your wrench. The displayed unit values are rounded separately, so use the matching displayed value rather than converting a rounded result again.

steps.title: Keep the setup consistent while tightening
steps.body: Use the same adapter direction, length and angle that you checked. Follow the component’s complete tightening sequence and any later angle stage. Recalculate or recheck the arrangement if you change tools or reposition the adapter.

diagnostics.finding: The adapter points away from the wrench handle.
diagnostics.meaning: The fastener is farther from your hand than the wrench drive is, changing the effective leverage.
diagnostics.next: Use the corresponding in-line calculator with the measured wrench and adapter lengths.

diagnostics.finding: The adapter points back toward the wrench handle.
diagnostics.meaning: The effective reach is shorter than the wrench length.
diagnostics.next: Use the reversed-arrangement calculator and confirm that adapter length is less than wrench length.

diagnostics.finding: A right-angle or wobble setup looks close to a listed arrangement.
diagnostics.meaning: Its no-correction guidance applies only when the actual geometry and any stated angle or length limits match.
diagnostics.next: Check the exact linked diagram, including the straight-adapter length limit or wobble-angle limit where applicable.

diagnostics.finding: Your half-moon adapter or wrench length is not selectable.
diagnostics.meaning: The available calculator does not establish a setting for that combination.
diagnostics.next: Use a supported setup that suits the job instead of substituting a nearby selection.

verification.title: Recheck the entries against the tools
verification.body: Confirm the target fastener torque, torque unit, handle-to-drive measurement, adapter measurement and chosen arrangement before using the displayed setting.

verification.title: Complete the component’s tightening instructions
verification.body: The corrected wrench setting addresses adapter leverage. Finish the specified tightening stages and component checks in the linked repair article for the job you are performing.

watchFor.title: Length measured from the wrong endpoints
watchFor.body: A is the distance from handle center to drive center. B is the distance between adapter centers. Including the adapter in A as well as B changes the calculation.

watchFor.title: Right-angle limits lost during repositioning
watchFor.body: A setup that begins at the illustrated angle may change when space gets tight. Repositioning the adapter changes the arrangement you checked.

guides.title: Replace the convertible tonneau-cover sensor assembly
guides.summary: Replace the affected D-tower cover and its integrated sensor, then check roof operation with the tonneau covers removed.
guides.introduction: Each optional tonneau cover contains a magnet that activates a Hall-effect sensor, an electronic switch responsive to a magnetic field. The roof control modules use these signals to prevent the convertible top from being raised with the covers installed. The sensor being serviced is part of the D-tower cover, so replacement means changing that assembly rather than removing a separate sensor.
guides.why: Cover detection is an operating interlock. A refusal to raise the roof may be correct behavior when a cover is fitted. Confirming the actual cover condition and other roof operating requirements helps avoid replacing a working assembly.

when.summary: When the integrated tonneau-cover sensor or its D-tower cover assembly has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Left and right sides use similar operations; replace the affected assembly.

prepare.title: Assembly and trim access
prepare.detail: Obtain the appropriate D-tower cover assembly. Have tools suitable for trim clips and pin-type retainers, and the convertible loadspace-trim procedure available.

prepare.title: Establish the complaint
prepare.detail: Note whether the tonneau covers are physically installed and which message appears. A cover-removal message with covers fitted is expected.

steps.title: Expose the affected side
steps.body: Remove the loadspace trim only as necessary using [Loadspace Trim Panel — Convertible](#/document/G1692610). Establish access to the connector and D-tower cover on the side being repaired.

steps.title: Disconnect the harness
steps.body: Disconnect the sensor harness connector before releasing the cover assembly. The connector operation is similar on both sides.

steps.title: Remove the D-tower cover
steps.body: Remove the bumper stop and the two pin-type retainers, then release the remaining clip and remove the cover. Follow [Tonneau Cover Sensor](#/document/G1723917) for the attachment locations.

steps.title: Install the complete replacement
steps.body: Reverse removal: engage the cover clip, restore the retainers and bumper stop, reconnect the harness and reinstall the disturbed loadspace trim. The sensor stays part of the replacement cover assembly.

watchFor.title: Confusing the two covers
watchFor.body: The removable tonneau cover carries the magnet; the D-tower cover contains the sensor being replaced.

notes: The roof switch must be held in the requested direction during roof movement.

diagnostics.finding: TOP DISABLED — REMOVE COVERS appears with a tonneau cover installed.
diagnostics.meaning: The roof is reporting an expected closing interlock.
diagnostics.next: Remove the tonneau covers before requesting roof raising.

diagnostics.finding: The same message appears with both covers removed.
diagnostics.meaning: The reported cover condition needs investigation; the message alone does not prove which sensor or circuit is responsible.
diagnostics.next: Establish the affected side and cause before replacing an assembly.

diagnostics.finding: The roof remains inoperative without a cover warning.
diagnostics.meaning: Roof operation also depends on accessory-delay status, vehicle speed and confirmation that both rear quarter windows are fully lowered.
diagnostics.next: Continue roof-system diagnosis rather than assuming the new sensor is defective.

verification.title: Check closing under valid conditions
verification.body: With the vehicle stationary, accessory delay active and tonneau covers removed, hold the UP switch. Confirm the windows lower and the roof raises.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record roof response and whether a cover-removal message remains despite both covers being physically removed.

guides.title: Replace the 3160 Manual Transmission Vehicle Speed Sensor
guides.summary: Replace the vehicle speed sensor on the 5.2L engine's 3160 manual transmission and secure its bolt and electrical connection.
guides.introduction: The vehicle speed sensor (VSS) works with a tone wheel in the transmission to turn rotational movement into an electrical speed signal. The 3160 transmission carries engine torque toward the rear differential, while this sensor provides information about rotation. The repair removes the externally accessible sensor through its electrical connector and retaining bolt.
guides.why: Safe underside access is the main preparation requirement. Once the sensor is reached, the specified bolt torque secures it in its mounting, and reconnecting the electrical connector restores the signal path. Replacing the sensor is a repair action; it does not by itself establish the cause of a speed-signal concern.

when.summary: When diagnosis or other transmission service requires removal or replacement of the VSS.
notes: Confirm the 3160 transmission application before following this procedure.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist positioned at the designated lifting points marked by stamped triangles. Check adapter clearance around suspension, steering, exhaust and underbody components. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the fastener tools
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the sensor bolt and a torque wrench capable of 71 lb.in (8 Nm). Be able to access and disconnect the sensor's electrical connector.

steps.title: Position the vehicle
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist. Follow [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631) for lifting-point and clearance requirements.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the sensor
steps.body: Locate the VSS using the [3160 sensor procedure](#/document/G1794239). Disconnect its electrical connector, then remove the retaining bolt and the sensor.

steps.title: Install the sensor
steps.body: Install the VSS and its retaining bolt. Tighten the bolt to 71 lb.in (8 Nm), using a torque wrench suited to this small-fastener specification.

steps.title: Restore the electrical connection
steps.body: Connect the VSS electrical connector after securing the sensor. Confirm the connection is complete before finishing the underside work.

watchFor.title: Wrong transmission application
watchFor.body: Use this sensor procedure for the 3160 transmission. Its identification tag is on the upper right side of the transmission.

watchFor.title: Torque-unit confusion
watchFor.body: Use the inch-pound scale for the specified bolt value. Choosing a foot-pound scale instead changes the applied torque.

notes: The sensor and its retaining bolt are separate service items from the internal speed-sensor tone wheel.

verification.title: Confirm installation
verification.body: Confirm the sensor is installed and its electrical connector is reconnected.

verification.title: Record the fastener result
verification.body: Record tightening of the VSS bolt to 71 lb.in (8 Nm).
