guides.title: Replace the fuel level sensor in the saddle-type tank
guides.summary: Drain the tank in stages, access both tank units and replace the fuel level sensor while protecting its connections and sealing surfaces.
guides.introduction: The fuel level sensor provides information about the fuel remaining in the tank. Its replacement requires more than opening its own access cover: the pump and sender unit must first be moved aside so remaining fuel can be removed from the left-hand saddle. This shared route applies to the listed engines, with separate pressure-release and coupling procedures for each.
guides.why: Pressure release and fuel removal solve different problems. Releasing pressure prepares the fuel connections for service; draining lowers fuel below the openings. Clean connections, undamaged seal contact surfaces and correctly aligned new seals are essential when closing the tank.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the separate fuel level sensor requires replacement.
notes: An incorrect level indication alone does not establish which component requires replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange fuel-service capability
prepare.detail: Use the 292-00004 Fuel Tanker 100 GPM and 310-123 fuel-tank lock-ring tool. This work requires controlled fuel transfer and access to the applicable pressure-release, battery and coupling procedures.

prepare.title: Prepare the drain connection and seals
prepare.detail: Have the supplemental refueling adapter from the luggage compartment and a 6 ft. length of 5/8 in. semi-rigid fuel drain tube. Arrange new seals for the opened pump/sender and fuel level sensor assemblies.

steps.title: Release pressure and disconnect the battery
steps.body: Follow the pressure-release procedure for the actual 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine first. Then disconnect the battery ground cable using the battery procedure.

steps.title: Withdraw fuel through the filler
steps.body: Insert the supplemental adapter and drain tube through the capless filler until the tube enters the tank. Connect the fuel tanker and remove as much fuel as possible, lowering fuel below the pump/sender flange and removing residual fuel from the filler pipe.

steps.title: Open the pump and sender access
steps.body: Remove the rear seat cushion and move the pump access cover aside. Disconnect the electrical connector and external fuel quick-release coupling. Carefully engage the lock-ring tool and remove the ring, then position the unit aside without damaging its float arm.

steps.title: Empty the left-hand saddle and inspect the seal area
steps.body: Use the tanker to completely drain remaining fuel from the left-hand saddle. Inspect the pump/sender flange and tank O-ring contact surfaces. Do not polish or adjust them; replace the affected unit or tank if the sealing area is bent, scratched or corroded. Remove and discard the O-ring.

steps.title: Release the fuel level sensor
steps.body: Move its access cover aside. Clean the connections, flange and immediate surrounding area before disconnecting the electrical connector. Carefully position the lock-ring tool and remove the sensor lock ring without damaging the sensor.

steps.title: Disconnect the internal fuel tube
steps.body: Release the internal tube-to-sensor quick-connect coupling using the engine-specific coupling procedure. This connection must be released before the sensor can be taken away without pulling on the internal tube.

steps.title: Reseal and reassemble
steps.body: Install a new fuel level sensor O-ring and make sure the sensor and tank alignment tabs meet before tightening its ring. Reverse the removal sequence, renewing the discarded pump/sender seal and restoring both units, their connections, access covers, rear cushion and battery connection.

steps.title: Prime the fuel system and check for leaks
steps.body: Finish the engine-specific fuel-pressure-release procedure’s restoration sequence. Reconnect the fuel-pump control-module connector used for pressure release; the 5.2L uses two connectors. Restore the rear seat cushion, cycle the ignition key and wait 3 seconds to pressurize the system. Check for leaks before starting the engine, then start it and check for leaks again. Keep this return-to-service check separate from confirming that the mechanical connections are latched.

watchFor.title: Damage during tool placement
watchFor.body: Careless lock-ring tool engagement can damage either tank unit. Protect the pump/sender float arm while positioning that unit aside.

watchFor.title: Contamination at the opening
watchFor.body: Clean around the sensor before opening its mounting so dirt is not carried into the tank or sealing joint.

notes: Keep pressure-release and quick-release coupling instructions matched to the engine throughout the job.

diagnostics.finding: A pump/sender or tank O-ring contact area is bent, scratched or corroded.
diagnostics.meaning: The sealing surface is unsuitable for reassembly.
diagnostics.next: Replace the affected pump/sender unit or tank; do not polish or reshape the contact area.

verification.title: Check assembly conditions
verification.body: Confirm new seals, sensor tab alignment before ring tightening, and restoration of all disconnected tubes and electrical connectors.

verification.title: Record the sealing decision
verification.body: Record flange condition, any component replacement required by damage, and renewal of the discarded and specified-new seals.

verification.title: Record both fuel-leak checks
verification.body: Confirm that the fuel-pump control-module connection or connections have been restored and that both the pre-start and running leak checks are complete.

guides.title: Replace a Two-Piston Front Brake Caliper
guides.summary: Disconnect and replace the two-piston front caliper, renew the brake-hose sealing washers and pressure bleed the brake system.
guides.introduction: The front brake caliper uses hydraulic pressure to press the brake pads against the disc. This procedure covers the two-piston caliper fitted to the listed 2.3L and 3.7L applications. Replacement involves opening the brake-hose connection and removing the guide-pin bolts, followed by reassembly and pressure bleeding.
guides.why: Opening the hose connection creates a route for fluid loss, contamination and air entry. The openings must remain sealed while disconnected, and the removed sealing washers must be discarded. Installing the replacement caliper restores the hardware; pressure bleeding completes the hydraulic part of the repair.
searchTerms: two piston front brake caliper replacement

when.summary: When a two-piston front brake caliper has been identified as requiring removal or replacement.
notes: Confirm the fitted caliper type before using this procedure.

prepare.title: Arrange wheel access and hydraulic equipment
prepare.detail: Have the capability to remove and reinstall the wheel safely, suitable means to seal hydraulic openings, new hose-connection washers and equipment for the referenced pressure-bleeding procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled tightening
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the flow bolt and guide-pin bolts, including a torque wrench. Follow the wheel procedure for its separate installation requirements.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and tire
steps.body: Follow [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) to expose the front caliper. Use the [two-piston caliper procedure](#/document/G1693776) to identify the hose connection and guide-pin fasteners.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the caliper
steps.body: Remove the brake-caliper flow bolt and disconnect the hose. Discard the washers and seal all openings. Then remove the two guide-pin bolts and the caliper, preserving the specified order of hydraulic disconnection before caliper removal.

steps.title: Install the replacement caliper
steps.body: Reverse removal. Tighten the guide-pin bolts to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm). Reconnect the hose using new washers and tighten the flow bolt to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm). Restore the wheel and tire according to their procedure.

steps.title: Pressure bleed the brake system
steps.body: Complete the referenced Brake System Pressure Bleeding procedure after installation. Tightening the connections does not remove air introduced while the hydraulic circuit was open.

watchFor.title: Unsealed hydraulic openings
watchFor.body: Keep all openings sealed while the hose and caliper are disconnected.

watchFor.title: Fluid on paintwork
watchFor.body: Immediately wash affected paintwork with cold water if brake fluid is spilled.

notes: The discarded parts specified here are the hose-connection washers.
Use the full pressure-bleeding procedure for its equipment, fluid and completion requirements.

verification.title: Confirm the installation details
verification.body: Verify new sealing washers were fitted and the flow bolt and guide-pin bolts were tightened to their respective specifications.

verification.title: Record hydraulic completion
verification.body: Record completion of the required pressure-bleeding procedure after caliper installation.

guides.title: Replace the crankshaft rear oil seal by engine variant
guides.summary: Renew the rear crankshaft oil seal using the correct retainer-sealing or seal-installation method for the fitted engine.
guides.introduction: The rear crankshaft seal retains engine oil where the rotating crankshaft exits toward the transmission. Access is behind the flywheel or flexplate. The 2.3L and 3.7L procedures include sealing a retainer joint, while the 5.0L and 5.2L procedures use tools to remove and seat the seal in its bore.
guides.why: A clean sealing surface and correctly seated seal are essential to containing oil. Retainer installation must preserve the applied silicone bead and meet its assembly deadline. The V8 crankshaft sensor ring needs careful handling, and the 5.2L seal has its own installation orientation.
searchTerms: oil leak at rear of engine

when.summary: When repair calls for replacement of the crankshaft rear oil seal after the leak source is established.
notes: Choose the engine branch before ordering parts or arranging installation tools.
Plan access through the applicable flywheel or flexplate procedure and its support requirements.

prepare.title: Prepare retainer-service materials
prepare.detail: For 2.3L and 3.7L work, obtain Motorcraft High Performance Engine RTV Silicone TA-357 and follow the sealing-surface preparation procedure. RTV means room-temperature-vulcanizing silicone. The 2.3L also needs installer 303-328, oil-drain equipment, a new oil filter and the specified engine oil.

prepare.title: Provide the V8 seal tools
prepare.detail: The 5.0L uses remover 303-519 with slide hammer 100-001. The 5.2L uses a universal seal puller. Both use installer 303-1250 with handle 205-153. Confirm replacement parts against engine identification.

prepare.title: Use the correct assembly lubricant
prepare.detail: The 3.7L specifies clean SAE 5W-20 synthetic-blend oil for the seal. The 5.0L specifies clean engine oil; the 5.2L specifies Motorcraft SAE 5W-50 Full Synthetic Motor Oil.

prepare.title: Arrange the required scan-tool completion
prepare.detail: On the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L, have a diagnostic scan tool capable of the specified misfire-monitor profile-correction routine. Flywheel or flexplate restoration includes this electronic completion step; a road test is a separate check.

steps.title: Expose the rear seal
steps.body: Remove the applicable flywheel or flexplate on the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L; remove the flywheel on the 5.2L. For the 3.7L and both V8s, remove the crankshaft sensor ring and engine-to-transmission spacer plate. Inspect the V8 sensor ring and discard it if dropped or visibly damaged.

steps.title: Remove the seal using the engine's method
steps.body: On the 3.7L, first disconnect and remove the crankshaft position (CKP) sensor, then remove the oil-pan-to-rear-seal bolts. On the 2.3L and 3.7L, unbolt and remove the rear-seal assembly and discard the seal; complete [RTV surface preparation](#/document/G1692003). On the 5.0L, use its specified remover and slide hammer. On the 5.2L, use a universal seal puller. Discard the removed seal in every branch.

steps.title: 2.3L: seal and install the retainer
steps.body: Follow [the 2.3L procedure](#/document/G1660464): apply a 3 mm silicone bead to the oil-pan surface and 5 mm beads at the T-joints. Fit installer 303-328. Introduce the retainer at an angle above the pan flange, then tilt it onto the block without scraping away sealant. Seat the seal, tighten the bolts in the illustrated sequence and remove the tool. Secure the assembly within 10 minutes; otherwise remove the sealant, clean and restart.

steps.title: 3.7L: complete its separate retainer procedure
steps.body: Follow [the 3.7L bead paths](#/document/G1681514) for the separate 5 mm and 3 mm silicone beads. Lubricate the seal with specified oil. Angle the retainer above the pan flange and tilt it onto the block, installing and tightening it within 10 minutes of sealant application. Tighten the retainer bolts in sequence and the oil-pan bolts through their torque-and-angle stages. Reinstall and reconnect the CKP sensor.

steps.title: 5.0L: install the lubricated seal
steps.body: Lubricate the seal bore and lips with clean engine oil. Position installer 303-1250 on the crankshaft, slide the new seal onto it and use handle 205-153 to install it through [the 5.0L procedure](#/document/G1685316).

steps.title: 5.2L: preserve the unique seal orientation
steps.body: Lubricate the retaining-plate bore and seal lips with specified 5W-50 oil. Position installer 303-1250, check the seal orientation in [the 5.2L installation detail](#/document/G1800269), and slide on the new seal. Install it using the specified handle and installer.

steps.title: Complete oil service and reassembly
steps.body: On the 2.3L, drain the oil after seal installation, refit the drain plug, discard the filter and fit a new filter with its seal lubricated. Follow the stated tightening instructions and refill using [2.3L oil specifications](#/document/G1660452). Restore the sensor ring and spacer plate on the applicable engines, then reinstall the correct flywheel or flexplate.

steps.title: Complete the engine-specific misfire-monitor routine
steps.body: After restoring the flywheel or flexplate, perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction with a diagnostic scan tool on the 3.7L and 5.0L. On the 5.2L, use the Powertrain Control Module (PCM) Misfire Monitor Profile Correction routine. Follow the relevant flywheel or flexplate procedure for that engine; do not transfer this requirement to the 2.3L branch.

steps.title: Road test after assembly and required electronic completion
steps.body: Perform the road test required by the selected rear-seal procedure after reassembly and any applicable profile-correction routine. Record the result separately from the scan-tool operation.

watchFor.title: Incorrect silicone on the 3.7L
watchFor.body: Use the specified Motorcraft sealant. The procedure warns that unsuitable sealant can cause excessive oil foaming and serious engine damage.

watchFor.title: Sealant scraped from the joint
watchFor.body: Preserve the angled retainer approach on the 2.3L and 3.7L so the oil-pan flange does not wipe away the bead.

notes: Use the tightening sequences and seal illustrations for the selected engine. The 5.2L seal orientation is unique to its procedure.

diagnostics.finding: A 5.0L or 5.2L crankshaft sensor ring was dropped or shows visible damage.
diagnostics.meaning: The ring is unsuitable for reuse under the stated inspection rule.
diagnostics.next: Discard it and install a replacement during reassembly.

verification.title: Confirm branch completion
verification.body: Confirm seal installation and surrounding reassembly against the selected procedure. Record completion of the required oil and filter change on the 2.3L.

verification.title: Record the applicable profile correction
verification.body: For the 3.7L and 5.0L, record completion of Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction. For the 5.2L, record the PCM Misfire Monitor Profile Correction result. Keep that record distinct from the subsequent road-test result.

verification.title: Record the road-test result
verification.body: Perform the required road test after reassembly and record the repair outcome and any remaining concern.

guides.title: Remove and replace the brake master cylinder
guides.summary: Remove the brake master cylinder, renew its mounting nuts and complete the bleeding branch appropriate to replacement or temporary removal.
guides.introduction: The brake master cylinder converts brake-pedal input into hydraulic pressure for the braking system. Its reservoir supplies fluid, and manual-transmission vehicles also have a clutch supply connection that must be addressed during removal. The job changes or temporarily removes the cylinder, opens hydraulic connections and therefore requires the appropriate bleeding work before completion.
guides.why: Air introduced into a hydraulic circuit can compress instead of transmitting pedal movement effectively. That makes bleeding part of the repair, not an optional final task. Sealing open connections protects the system from contamination, and the cylinder’s mounting nuts must be replaced after removal.

when.summary: When the master cylinder requires replacement or must be removed to reach another component.
notes: Choose the bleeding route according to whether a new cylinder is installed or the original cylinder is refitted.
Manual-transmission vehicles also require clutch bleeding.

prepare.title: Arrange hydraulic-service capability
prepare.detail: Have the applicable bleeding procedures and equipment ready before opening the system. For manual-transmission vehicles, provide a suitable suction device for emptying the reservoir.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement nuts and closures
prepare.detail: Obtain new master-cylinder mounting nuts, suitable closures for hydraulic openings, and torque tools for the mounting nuts and brake-tube fittings.

prepare.title: Protect painted surfaces
prepare.detail: If brake fluid reaches paintwork, wash the affected area immediately with cold water.

steps.title: Disconnect the manual-transmission supply branch
steps.body: On manual-transmission vehicles, remove the reservoir cap and siphon out the brake fluid with a suitable suction device. Disconnect the clutch master-cylinder tube and detach its bracket from the master-cylinder studs.

steps.title: Release the electrical and brake connections
steps.body: On all vehicles, disconnect the fluid-level sensor connector and detach the harness retainer from the reservoir. Disconnect the two brake-tube fittings, ensuring all openings are sealed.

steps.title: Remove the cylinder and discard its nuts
steps.body: Remove the two mounting nuts and the brake master cylinder. Discard both nuts; the [removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1692560) requires replacement fasteners.

steps.title: Reinstall the cylinder and connections
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence using new mounting nuts. Tighten the nuts to 23 Nm and the brake-tube fittings to 27.5 Nm. Restore the sensor connector, harness retainer and, where applicable, the clutch tube, bracket and reservoir cap.

steps.title: Complete the correct bleeding operations
steps.body: For a new cylinder, follow [Component Bleeding](#/document/G1694693) to bleed the master cylinder. If the original cylinder was removed for access and refitted, follow Brake System Pressure Bleeding. Manual-transmission vehicles additionally require clutch bleeding.

steps.title: Complete the replacement check
steps.body: When a new master cylinder has been installed, road-test the vehicle after the required bleeding work is complete. Record that result separately from the hydraulic assembly work.

watchFor.title: Open hydraulic ports
watchFor.body: Keep all disconnected openings sealed. Leaving them exposed defeats the contamination precaution required during removal.

watchFor.title: Reused mounting nuts
watchFor.body: Do not reinstall the discarded cylinder mounting nuts.

notes: Manual-transmission vehicles need clutch bleeding after the hydraulic supply has been opened. The linked procedure is used by both MT82 and 3160 installation instructions; follow it with the fitted gearbox’s restoration requirements.
Use the complete named Brake System Pressure Bleeding procedure when refitting a cylinder removed for access; no substitute bleeding sequence is given here.

diagnostics.finding: A new master cylinder is being installed.
diagnostics.meaning: The replacement branch requires master-cylinder bleeding and a road test.
diagnostics.next: Complete Component Bleeding, any applicable clutch bleeding and the road test.

diagnostics.finding: The original cylinder is being refitted after access work.
diagnostics.meaning: The procedure directs brake-system pressure bleeding.
diagnostics.next: Complete that bleeding route and clutch bleeding if the vehicle has a manual transmission.

verification.title: Confirm assembly completion
verification.body: Confirm new mounting nuts, tightened tube fittings, restored electrical connections and the applicable clutch supply attachments.

verification.title: Record the hydraulic completion route
verification.body: Record whether the cylinder was renewed or reused, which bleeding operations were completed, and the road-test result when replacement required it.
